There is a lamp inside the house, its light is visible from outside. Similarly elsewhere the light of a gem is seen (from outside).

Chapter 9 · Verse 4

9.4

दूरे प्रभाद्वयं दृष्ट्वा मणिबुद्ध्याभिधावतोः। प्रभायां मणिबुद्धिस्तु मिथ्याज्ञानं द्वयोरपि॥

On seeing the two gleams at a distance, both (the men) took them for gems and ran after them. Their notions are equally wrong, in that they took the gleams for gems.

Chapter 9 · Verse 5

9.5

न लभ्यते मणिर्दीपप्रभां प्रत्यभिधावता। प्रभायां धावतावश्यं लभ्यतैव मणिर्मणेः॥

The man who ran for the gleam of the lamp did not find the gem, but the man who ran for the gleam of the gem got it.

Chapter 9 · Verse 6

9.6

दीपप्रभामणिभ्रान्तिर्विसंवादिभ्रमः स्मृतः। मणिप्रभामणिभ्रान्तिः संवादिभ्रम उच्यते॥

Mistaking the gleam of a lamp for a gem is called a Visaṃvādi-Bhrama, ‘misleading error’ (or an error that does not lead to the goal). Mistaking the gleam of a gem for a gem is called a ‘leading’ or ‘informative’ error, though both are errors (or wrong observations).

Chapter 9 · Verse 7

9.7

बाष्पं धूमतया बुध्वा तत्राङ्गारानुमानतः। वह्निर्यदृच्छया लब्धः स संवादिभ्रमो मतः॥

On seeing a mist and mistaking it for smoke, if a man argues the existence of fire there and goes for getting charcoal and accidentally finds it, his mistake is called a ‘leading’ error, a chance coincidence.

Chapter 9 · Verse 8

9.8

गोदावर्युदकं गङ्गोदकं मत्वा विशुद्धये। सम्प्रोक्ष्य शुद्धिमाप्नोति स संवादिभ्रमो मतः॥

Sprinkling on himself the water of the River Godāvarī thinking it to be that of the River Ganges, if a man is actually purified this is ‘leading’ error (Saṃvādi-Bhrama).

Chapter 9 · Verse 9

9.9

ज्वरेणाप्तः सन्निपातं भ्रान्त्या नारायणं स्मरन्। मृतः स्वर्गमवाप्नोति स संवादिभ्रमो मतः॥

A man suffering from a high fever repeats ‘Nārāyaṇa’ in delirium and dies. He goes to heaven. This is again a ‘leading’ error.

Chapter 9 · Verse 10

9.10

प्रत्यक्षस्यानुमानस्य तथा शास्त्रस्य गोचरे। उक्तन्यायेन संवादिभ्रमाः सन्तीह कोटिशः॥

In direct perception, in inference and in the application of scriptural authority, there are innumerable instances of such leading errors or chance coincidences.

Chapter 9 · Verse 11

9.11

अन्यथा मृत्तिकादारुशिलाः स्युर्देवताः कथम्। अग्नित्वादिधियोपास्याः कथं वा योषिदादयः॥

Otherwise, how could images of clay, wood and stone be worshipped as deities or how could a woman be worshipped as fire?

Chapter 9 · Verse 12

9.12

अयथावस्तुविज्ञानात्फलं लभ्यत ईप्सितम्। काकतालीयतः सोऽयं संवादिभ्रम उच्यते॥

From the knowledge and (or) adoption of a wrong means, sometimes, by accident, as in the sitting of a crow on the branch of a palm tree and in the instantaneous fall of a fruit thereof, a desired result is obtained. This knowledge and (or) adoption of a wrong means is called a Saṃvādi-Bhrama or a ‘leading’ error, or error leading to a right knowledge.

Chapter 9 · Verse 13

9.13

स्वयं भ्रमोऽपि संवादी यथा सम्यक्फलप्रदः। ब्रह्मतत्त्वोपासनापि तथा मुक्तिफलप्रदा॥

The ‘leading’ error though a wrong notion is potent enough to give the correct result. So also the meditation or worship of Brahman leads to liberation.

Chapter 9 · Verse 14

9.14

वेदान्तेभ्यो ब्रह्मतत्त्वमखण्डैकरसात्मकम्। परोक्षमवगम्यैतदहमस्मीत्युपासते॥

After indirectly knowing the one indivisible homogeneous Brahman from the books on Vedānta, one should meditate on or think repeatedly ‘I am Brahman’.

Chapter 9 · Verse 15

9.15

प्रत्यग्व्यक्तिमनुल्लिख्य शास्त्राद्विष्ण्वादिमूर्तिवत्। अस्ति ब्रह्मेति सामान्यज्ञानमत्रं परोक्षधीः॥

Without realising Brahman to be one’s own Self, the general knowledge of Him derived through the study of the scriptures, viz., ‘Brahman is’, is here called indirect knowledge, just as our knowledge of the forms of Viṣṇu etc., is called.

Chapter 9 · Verse 16

9.16

चतुर्भुजाद्यवगतावपि मूर्तिमनुल्लिखन्। अक्षैः परोक्षज्ञान्येव न तदा विष्णुमीक्षते॥

One may have knowledge of Viṣṇu from scriptures as having four arms etc., but if one does not have a vision of Him, he is said to have only indirect knowledge, inasmuch as he has not seen Him with his eyes.

Chapter 9 · Verse 17

9.17

परोक्षत्वापराधेन भवेन्नातत्त्ववेदनम्। प्रमाणेनैव शास्त्रेण सत्यमूर्तेर्विभासनात्॥

This knowledge because of its defect of indirectness is not false, for the true form of Viṣṇu has been revealed by the scriptures which are authoritative.

Chapter 9 · Verse 18

9.18

सच्चिदानन्दरूपस्य शास्त्राद्भानेऽप्यनुल्लिखन्। प्रत्यंचं साक्षिणं तत्तु ब्रह्म साक्षान्न वीक्षते॥

From the scripture a man may have a conception of Brahman as existence, consciousness and bliss but he cannot have a direct knowledge of Brahman unless Brahman is cognised as the inner witness in his own personality.

Chapter 9 · Verse 19

9.19

शास्त्रोक्तेनैव मार्गेण सच्चिदानन्दनिर्णयात्। परोक्षमपि तज्ज्ञानं तत्त्वज्ञानं न तु भ्रमः॥

As the knowledge of Sat-Cit-Ānanda has been acquired in the scriptural method, it, though an indirect knowledge, is not an illusory one.

Chapter 9 · Verse 20

9.20

ब्रह्म यद्यपि शास्त्रेषु प्रत्यक्त्वेनैव वर्णितम्। महावाक्यैस्तथाप्येतद्दुर्बोधमविचारिणः॥

Though Brahman has been described as being one’s own Self in the scriptures and the great Saying, still, one cannot understand It without the practice of enquiry.

Chapter 9 · Verse 21

9.21

देहाद्यात्मत्वविभ्रान्तौ जागृत्यां न हठात्पुमान्। ब्रह्मात्मत्वेन विज्ञातुं क्षमते मन्दधीत्वतः॥

As long as the delusion that the body is the Self, is strong in a man of dull intellect, he is not able at once to know Brahman as the Self.

Chapter 9 · Verse 22

9.22

ब्रह्ममात्रं सुविज्ञेयं श्रद्धालोः शास्त्रदर्शिनः। अपरोक्षद्वैतबुद्धिः परोक्षद्वैतबुद्ध्यनुत्॥

As the perception of duality is not opposed to an indirect knowledge of non-duality, a man of faith, expert in the scriptures, can easily have the indirect knowledge of Brahman.

Chapter 9 · Verse 23

9.23

अपरोक्षशिलाबुद्धिर्न परोक्षेशतां नुदेत्। प्रतिमादिषु विष्णुत्वे को वा विप्रतिपद्यते॥

The perception of a stone image is not opposed to an indirect knowledge of the deity whom the image represents. Which devotee contradicts the idea of Viṣṇu in the image?

Chapter 9 · Verse 24

9.24

अश्रद्धालोरविश्वासोः नोदाहरणमर्हति। श्रद्धालोरेव सर्वत्र वैदिकेष्वधिकारतः॥

The disbelief of those who have no faith need not be considered, for the believing alone are authorised to perform the Vedic actions.

Chapter 9 · Verse 25

9.25

सकृदाप्तोपदेशेन परोक्षज्ञानमुद्भवेत्। विष्णुमूर्त्युपदेशो हि न मीमांसामपेक्षते॥

An indirect knowledge of Brahman can arise even through a single instruction by a competent teacher. It is like the knowledge of the form of Viṣṇu which does not depend on intellectual enquiry.

Chapter 9 · Verse 26

9.26

कर्मोपास्ती विचार्येतेऽनुष्ठेयाविनिर्णयात्। बहुशाखाविप्रकीर्णं निर्णेतुं कः प्रभुर्नरः॥

As there may be doubts about them, ritualistic works and methods of worship have been discussed (in the scriptures). Who otherwise could have synthesised the directions about them, scattered as they are over many branches of the Vedas?

Chapter 9 · Verse 27

9.27

निर्णितोऽर्थः कल्पसूत्रैर्ग्रथितस्तावतास्तिकः। विचारमन्तरेणापि शक्तोऽनुष्ठातुमञ्जसा॥

Such rituals and methods of worship have been collected and co-ordinated in the Kalpa-Sūtras. With their help man, who has faith, may practise them without further enquiry.

Chapter 9 · Verse 28

9.28

उपास्तीनामनुष्ठानमार्षग्रन्थेषु वर्णितम्। विचाराक्षममर्त्याश्च तत्श्रुत्वोपासते गुरोः॥

The methods of worship are described in other works by the seers. Those who are dull of ratiocination go to a teacher and learn the methods from him.

Chapter 9 · Verse 29

9.29

वेदवाक्यानि निर्णेतुमिच्छन्मीमांसतां जनः। आप्तोपदेशमन्त्रेण ह्यनुष्ठानं तु सम्भवेत्॥

To determine the correct meaning of the Vedic texts let the learned resort to enquiry, but practical worship can be performed (with benefit) according to the teachings of a competent teacher.

Chapter 9 · Verse 30

9.30

ब्रह्मसाक्षात्कृतिस्त्वेवं विचारेण विना नृणाम्। आप्तोपदेशमात्रेण न सम्भवति कुत्रचित्॥

The direct realisation of Brahman, however, is never possible only from the instructions of a competent teacher without the practice of inquiry (vicāra).

Chapter 9 · Verse 31

9.31

परोक्षज्ञानमश्रद्धा प्रतिबध्नाति नेतरत्। अविचारोऽपरोक्षस्य ज्ञानस्य प्रतिबन्धकः॥

Want of faith alone obstructs the indirect knowledge; want of enquiry is however the obstacle to the direct knowledge.

Chapter 9 · Verse 32

9.32

विचाराप्यपरोक्षेण ब्रह्मात्मानं न वेत्ति चेत्। आपरोक्ष्यावसानत्वाद्भूयोभूयो विचारयेत्॥

If even by enquiry one does not get the direct knowledge of Brahman as the Self, one should repeatedly practise enquiry, for enquiry, it is prescribed, should continue until direct knowledge dawns.

Chapter 9 · Verse 33

9.33

विचारयन्नामरणं नैवात्मानं लभेत चेत्। जन्मान्तरे लभेतैव प्रतिबन्धक्षये सति॥

If a person does not realise the Self even after practising till death, he will surely realise it in a future life when all the obstacles will have been eliminated.

Chapter 9 · Verse 34

9.34

इह वामुत्र वा विद्येत्येवं सूत्रकृतोदितम्। शृण्वन्तोऽप्यत्र बहवो यन्न विद्युरिति श्रुतिः॥

Knowledge will arise either in this birth or the next, says the author of the Brahma Sūtras. The Śruti also says that there are many who listen to the teachings on non-duality and yet do not realise in this life.

Chapter 9 · Verse 35

9.35

गर्भ एव शयानः सन्वामदेवोऽवबुद्धवान्। पूर्वाभ्यस्तविचारेण यद्वदध्ययनादिषु॥

By virtue of the practice of spiritual enquiry in a previous birth, Vāma-deva had realisation even while in his mother’s womb. Such results are also seen in the case of studies.

Chapter 9 · Verse 36

9.36

बहुवारमधीतेऽपि तदा नायाति चेत्पुनः। दिनान्तरेऽनधीत्यैव पूर्वाधीतं स्मरेत्पुमान्॥

In spite of reading many times a boy may not be able to memorise something, but sometimes, next morning, without any further study, he remembers all that he has read.

Chapter 9 · Verse 37

9.37

कालेन परिपच्यन्ते कृषिदर्भादयो यथा। तद्वदात्मविचारोऽपि शनैः कालेन पच्यते॥

As the seed in the field or in the womb matures in time, so in the course of time the practice of self-enquiry gradually ripens and bears fruit.

Chapter 9 · Verse 38

9.38

पुनःपुनर्विचारोऽपि त्रिविधप्रतिबन्धतः। न वेत्ति तत्त्वमित्येतद्वार्तिके सम्यगीरितम्॥

In spite of repeated enquiry a man does not realise the truth because of three kinds of impediments. This has been clearly pointed out in his Vārtika by Ācārya Sureśvara.

Chapter 9 · Verse 39

9.39

कुतस्तज्ज्ञानमिति चेत्तद्धि बन्धपरिक्षयात्। असावपि च भूतो वा भावी वा वर्तते तथा॥

If you ask why the realisation (which did not arise before) comes now, we shall reply that knowledge comes only with the total removal of impediments which may be past, present or future.

Chapter 9 · Verse 40

9.40

अधीतवेदवेदार्थोऽप्यत एव न मुच्यते। हिरण्यनिधिदृष्टान्तादिदमेव हि दर्शितम्॥

Therefore only by studying the Veda and its meaning a man is not released. This has been shown in the example of hidden gold.

Chapter 9 · Verse 41

9.41

अतीतेनापि महिषीस्नेहेन प्रतिबन्धतः। भिक्षुस्तत्त्वं न वेदेति गाथा लोके प्रगीयते॥

There is the popular song saying that a monk could not realise the truth, the impediment being his past attachment to his queen (or a she-buffalo, mahiṣī).

Chapter 9 · Verse 42

9.42

अनुसृत्य गुरुः स्नेहं महिष्यां तत्त्वमुक्तवान्। ततो यथावद्वेदैष प्रतिबन्धस्य संक्षयात्॥

His teacher instructed him of Brahman knowing his attachment to her (by telling him that Brahman was her substratum). When the impediment was removed, the monk realised the truth properly.

Chapter 9 · Verse 43

9.43

प्रतिबन्धो वर्तमानो विषयासक्तिलक्षणः। प्रज्ञामान्द्यं कुतर्कश्च विपर्ययदुराग्रहः॥

The impediments of the present are (i) binding attachment to the objects of the senses, (ii) dullness of the intellect, (iii) indulgence in improper and illogical arguments and (iv) the deep conviction that the Self is an agent and an enjoyer.

Chapter 9 · Verse 44

9.44

शमाद्यैः श्रवणाद्यैश्च तत्र तत्रोचितैः क्षयम्। नीतेऽस्मिन्प्रतिबन्धेऽतः स्वस्य ब्रह्मत्वमश्नुते॥

Through the practice of inner control and other qualifications and through hearing the truth and so forth, suitable for counteracting the impediments, the latter slowly perish and one realises his Self as Brahman.

Chapter 9 · Verse 45

9.45

आगामिप्रतिबन्धश्च वामदेवे समीरितः। एकेन जन्मना क्षीणो भरतस्य त्रिजन्मभिः॥

The future impediment has been well illustrated in the case of Vāma-deva. He overcame it in one birth and Bharata in three births.

Chapter 9 · Verse 46

9.46

योगभ्रष्टस्य गीतायामतीते बहुजन्मनि। प्रतिबन्धक्षयः प्रोक्तो न विचारोऽप्यनर्थकः॥

In the Gītā, it has been told that a Yogī who has not attained illumination in this life may be freed from the impediment after many births. Yet his practice of enquiry is never fruitless.

Chapter 9 · Verse 47

9.47

प्राप्य पुण्यकृतां लोकानात्मतत्त्वविचारतः। शुचीनां श्रीमतां गेहे योगभ्रष्टोऽभिजायते॥

Because of his practice of enquiry such a Yogī enters into the heaven of the meritorious and then if he is not freed from desires, he is born again in a pious and prosperous family.

Chapter 9 · Verse 48

9.48

अथवा योगिनामेव कुले भवति धीमताम्। निस्पृहः ब्रह्मतत्त्वस्य विचारात्तद्धि दुर्लभम्॥

Or, if he has no worldly desires, he is born in a family of Yogīs who have pure intellect due to their practice of enquiry into the nature of Brahman, for such a birth is hard to obtain.

Chapter 9 · Verse 49

9.49

तत्र तं बुद्धिसंयोगं लभते पौर्वदेहिकम्। यतते च ततो भूयस्तस्मादेतद्धि दुर्लभम्॥

He regains the Yogic intellect acquired in his previous birth and so strives more vigorously; this birth is indeed hard to achieve.

Chapter 9 · Verse 50

9.50

पूर्वाभ्यासेन तेनैव ह्रियते ह्यवशोऽपि सः। अनेकजन्मसंसिद्धस्ततो याति परां गतिम्॥

He is borne on by the momentum of his Yogic practices in the previous birth even against his inclination. Thus after many births he achieves perfection and as a result is liberated.

Chapter 9 · Verse 51

9.51

ब्रह्मलोकाभिवाञ्छायां सम्यक्सत्यां निरुध्यताम्। विचारयेद्य आत्मानं न तु साक्षात्करोत्ययम्॥

A man who has a strong desire for Brahma-loka, but suppresses it and practises enquiry about the Self, will not have realisation.

Chapter 9 · Verse 52

9.52

वेदान्तविज्ञानसुनिश्चितार्थाः इति शास्त्रतः। ब्रह्मलोके सकल्पान्ते ब्रह्मणा सह मुच्यते॥

As the scriptures say, the monk, who has well ascertained the meaning of Vedānta, goes to the realm of Brahmā and is released at the end of the four Yugas along with Brahmā.

Chapter 9 · Verse 53

9.53

केषांचित्स विचारोऽपि कर्मणा प्रतिबद्ध्यते। श्रवणायापि बहुभिर्यो न लभ्य इति श्रुतेः॥

In some cases the enquiry itself is impeded because of the result of their evil deeds as the Śruti says: ‘Even to hear about Him it is not available to many’.

Chapter 9 · Verse 54

9.54

अत्यन्तबुद्धिमान्द्याद्वा सामग्र्या वाप्यसम्भवात्। यो विचारं न लभते ब्रह्मोपासीत सोऽनिशम्॥

If a man cannot practise enquiry, either due to extreme dullness of intellect or for want of other favourable circumstances, let him always keep the mind on Brahman.

Chapter 9 · Verse 55

9.55

निर्गुणब्रह्मतत्त्वस्य न ह्युपास्तेरसम्भवः। सगुणब्रह्मणीवात्र प्रत्ययावृत्तिसम्भवात्॥

As it is possible to continue the thought-current regarding Brahman with attributes, meditation on the attributeless Brahman also is not impossible.

Chapter 9 · Verse 56

9.56

अवाङ्मनसगम्यं तन्नोपास्यमिति चेत्तदा। अवाङ्मनसगम्यस्य वेदनं च न सम्भवेत्॥

(Doubt): Brahman is beyond speech and mind and so cannot be meditated upon. (Reply): Then there can be no knowledge of Brahman too.

Chapter 9 · Verse 57

9.57

वागाद्यगोचराकारमित्येवं यदि वेत्त्यसौ। वागाद्यगोचराकारमित्युपासित नो कुतः॥

(Doubt): Brahman is known as beyond speech and mind. (Reply): Then why cannot Brahman be meditated upon as beyond speech and mind?

Chapter 9 · Verse 58

9.58

सगुणत्वमुपास्यत्वाद्यदि वेद्यत्वतोऽपि तत्। वेद्यं चेल्लक्षणावृत्त्या लक्षितं समुपास्यताम्॥

(Doubt): If Brahman can be meditated upon He becomes invested with attributes. (Reply): That happens if He is taken as knowable. (Doubt): Brahman is knowable by Lakṣaṇa, indirect indication. (Reply): Then meditate upon Brahman that way, i.e., by Lakṣaṇa.

Chapter 9 · Verse 59

9.59

ब्रह्म विद्धि तदेव त्वं नत्विदं यदुपासते। इति श्रुतेरुपास्यत्वं निषिद्धं ब्रह्मणो यदि॥

(Doubt): The Śruti saying, ‘Know that alone to be Brahman which is beyond the range of speech and mind and not that which the people worship’, prohibits meditation on Brahman.

Chapter 9 · Verse 60

9.60

विदितादन्यदेवेति श्रुतेर्वेद्यत्वमस्य न। यथा श्रुत्यैव वेद्यं तत्तथा श्रुत्याप्युपास्यताम्॥

(Reply): Equally Brahman cannot be an object of knowledge, for the Śruti says: ‘Brahman is other than that which can be known’. (Doubt): The Śruti also says that Brahman can be known. (Reply): So also it says that He can be meditated upon. So meditate on Him basing upon those Vedic texts.

Chapter 9 · Verse 61

9.61

विदितादन्यदेवेति श्रुतेर्वेद्यत्वमस्य न। यथा श्रुत्यैव वेद्यं तत्तथा श्रुत्याप्युपास्यताम्॥

(Doubt): But Brahman as an object of knowledge is unreal. (Reply): Why not as an object of meditation too? (Doubt): Covering and apprehending by Vṛttis is knowledge. (Reply): Similarly, doing that is meditation.

Chapter 9 · Verse 62

9.62

का ते भक्तिरुपास्तौ चेत्कस्ते द्वेषस्तदीरय। मानाभावो न वाच्योऽस्यां बहुश्रुतिषु दर्शनात्॥

(Doubt): Why are you so devoted to meditation on the attributeless Brahman? (Reply): Why are you so opposed to it? Say that. As there are many Śruti texts prescribing meditation on the attributeless Brahman, it is not proper to say that there is no authority for it.

Chapter 9 · Verse 63

9.63

उत्तरस्मिंस्तापनीये शैब्यप्रश्नेऽथ काठके। माण्डुक्यादौ च सर्वत्र निर्गुणोपास्तिरीरिता॥

Meditation on the attributeless Brahman has been prescribed in the Nṛsiṃha-Uttara-Tāpanīya, Praśna (Śaibya’s fifth question), Kāṭha, Māṇḍukya and other Upaniṣads.

Chapter 9 · Verse 64

9.64

अनुष्ठानप्रकारोऽस्याः पञ्चीकरण ईरितः। ज्ञानसाधनमेतच्चेन्नेति केनात्र वर्णितम्॥

This method of meditation of the attributeless Brahman has been in the Pañcīkaraṇa Vārtika by Sureśvara. (Doubt): This meditation is the means of indirect knowledge of Brahman (but not of liberation). (Reply): We don’t say that it is not so.

Chapter 9 · Verse 65

9.65

नानुतिष्ठति कोऽप्येतदिति चेन्नानुतिष्ठतु। पुरुषस्यापराधेन किमुपास्तिः प्रदुष्यति॥

(Doubt): But most of the people do not practise this type of meditation. (Reply): Let them not do. How can the meditation be blamed for the short-comings of the meditator?

Chapter 9 · Verse 66

9.66

इतोऽप्यतिशयं मत्वा मन्त्रान्वश्यादिकारिणः। मूढा जपन्तु तेभ्योऽतिमूढाः कृषिमुपासताम्॥

People of spiritually dull intellect repeat sacred formulas to acquire power over others, finding it more immediately fruitful than meditation on Brahman with attributes. There are people still more dull-witted who concentrate only on agriculture.

Chapter 9 · Verse 67

9.67

तिष्ठन्तु मूढाः प्रकृता निर्गुणोपास्तिरीर्यते। विद्यैक्यात्सर्वशाखास्थान्गुणानत्रोपसंहरेत्॥

Let the dull-witted do what they like! Here we speak of meditation on the Absolute. Since it is of one Vidyā or Upāsana, all the qualifications of Brahman described in the various branches of the Veda must be gathered for meditation.

Chapter 9 · Verse 68

9.68

आनन्दादेर्विधेयस्य गुणसङ्घस्य संहृतिः। आनन्दादय इत्यस्मिन्सूत्रे व्यासेन वर्णिता॥

The positive qualities of bliss etc., are all to be co-ordinated into meditation on Brahman. This has been told by Vyāsa in the ‘Ānandādaya..’ Sūtra.

Chapter 9 · Verse 69

9.69

अस्थूलादेर्निषेध्यस्य गुणसङ्घस्य संहृतिः। तथा व्यासेन सूत्रेऽस्मिनुक्ताक्षरधियान्त्विति॥

Similarly Vyāsa speaks of all the negative indications of Brahman such as ‘not gross’ in the ‘Akṣaradhiyam’ Sūtra.

Chapter 9 · Verse 70

9.70

निर्गुणब्रह्मतत्त्वस्य विद्यायां गुणसंहृतिः। न युज्येतेत्युपालम्भो व्यासं प्रत्येव मां तु न॥

(Doubt): Combining and thinking of these indications do not fit in with meditation on the attributeless Brahman. (Reply): Then your doubt is directed against Vyāsa himself and not against me alone.

Chapter 9 · Verse 71

9.71

हिरण्यस्मश्रुसूर्यादिमूर्तीनामनुदाहृतेः। अविरुद्धं निर्गुणत्वमिति चेत्तुष्यतां त्वया॥

(Doubt): As (Vyāsa) has not asked for the inclusion of the forms such as of the sun with golden beard etc., meditation on the attributeless is not contradicted. (Reply): Be satisfied with that; we also do not ask for that.

Chapter 9 · Verse 72

9.72

गुणानां लक्षकत्वेन न तत्त्वेऽन्तःप्रवेशनम्। इति चेदस्त्वेवमेव ब्रह्मतत्त्वमुपास्यताम्॥

(Doubt): Qualities are only indirect indications; they cannot enter into the true nature of Brahman. (Reply): Let them be so. Meditate on Brahman thus indicated.

Chapter 9 · Verse 73

9.73

आनन्दादिभिरस्थूलादिभिःस्वात्मात्र लक्षितः। अखण्डैकरसः सोऽहमस्मीत्येवमुपासते॥

The Self is here indirectly indicated by positive qualities like ‘bliss’ etc., and by negative qualities like ‘not gross’ etc. One should meditate on the indivisible, homogeneous Self as ‘That I am’.

Chapter 9 · Verse 74

9.74

आनन्दादिभिरस्थूलादिभिःस्वात्मात्र लक्षितः। अखण्डैकरसः सोऽहमस्मीत्येवमुपासते॥

(Doubt): What is the difference between knowledge and meditation? (Reply): Listen; knowledge depends on the object, whereas meditation depends on the will of the person meditating.

Chapter 9 · Verse 75

9.75

विचाराज्जायते बोधोऽनिच्छा यं न निवर्तयेत्। स्वोत्पत्तिमात्रात्संसारे दहत्यखिलसत्यताम्॥

By the practice of enquiry, the knowledge of Brahman arises; then it cannot be prevented whether one likes it or not. Such knowledge, by the mere fact of its arising, destroys all ideas of the reality of the world.

Chapter 9 · Verse 76

9.76

तावता कृतकृत्यः सन्नित्यतृप्तिमुपागतः। जीवन्मुक्तिमनुप्राप्य प्रारब्धक्षयमीक्षते॥

On acquiring knowledge the aspirant experiences unbroken satisfaction and a feeling of having accomplished all that was to be accomplished. He becomes liberated in life and awaits the wearing-out of his fructifying Karma.

Chapter 9 · Verse 77

9.77

आप्तोपदेशं विश्वस्य श्रद्धालुरविचारयन्। चिन्तयेत्प्रत्ययैरन्यैरनन्तरितवृत्तिभिः॥

On the other hand, a believing man, putting his faith in the teachings of his teacher and without practising enquiry, should meditate on the object prescribed without being distracted by other thoughts.

Chapter 9 · Verse 78

9.78

यावच्चिन्त्यस्वरूपत्वाभिमानः स्वस्य जायते। तावद्विचिन्त्य पश्चाच्च तथैवामृति धारयेत्॥

He should continue the practice of meditation until he realises himself to be identical with his object of meditation and then continue this thought till death.

Chapter 9 · Verse 79

9.79

ब्रह्मचारी भिक्षमाणो युतः संवर्गविद्यया। संवर्गरूपतां चित्ते धारयित्वा ह्यभिक्षता॥

A certain Brahma-cārī used to go for alms keeping in his mind his identity with the vital air within him.

Chapter 9 · Verse 80

9.80

पुरुषस्वेच्छया कर्तुमकर्तुं कर्तुमन्यथा। शक्योपास्तिरतो नित्यं कुर्यात्प्रत्ययसन्ततिम्॥

Meditation depends on the will of a man whether he is to do or not to do or to do it in a different way. One should therefore always continue the thought current.

Chapter 9 · Verse 81

9.81

वेदाध्यायी ह्यप्रमत्तोऽधीते स्वप्नेऽपि वासितः। जपिता तु जपत्येव तथा ध्यातापि वासयेत्॥

A student, diligent in reciting the Vedas, reads or recites them even in his dreams through the force of habit. Similarly, one who practises meditation, continues it even in his dreams.

Chapter 9 · Verse 82

9.82

विरोधिप्रत्ययं त्यक्त्वा नैरन्तर्येण भावयन्। लभते वासनावेशात्स्वप्नादावपि भावनाम्॥

Giving up contrary thoughts, if a man ceaselessly meditates, he meditates even in his dreams because of the deep impression.

Chapter 9 · Verse 83

9.83

भुञ्जानोऽपि निज आरब्धमास्थातिशयतोऽनिशम्। ध्यातुं शक्तो न सन्देहो विषयव्यसनी यथा॥

There is no doubt that while experiencing the results of his fructifying Karma a man, because of his strong impression, is able to meditate without intermission, just as a man attached to worldly objects always thinks of them.

Chapter 9 · Verse 84

9.84

परव्यसनिनी नारी व्यग्रापि गृहकर्मणि। तदेवास्वादयत्यन्तः परसङ्गरसायनम्॥

A woman devoted to a paramour, though engaged in household duties, will all the time be dwelling in mind on the pleasures with him.

Chapter 9 · Verse 85

9.85

परसङ्गं स्वादयन्त्या अपि नो गृहकर्म तत्। कुण्ठी भवेदपि त्वेतदापातेनैव वर्तते॥

While enjoying in mind the pleasure of the company of her lover, her household duties though not much disturbed, are managed indifferently.

Chapter 9 · Verse 86

9.86

गृहकृत्यव्यसनिनी यथा सम्यक्करोति तत्। परव्यसनिनी तद्वन्न करोत्येव सर्वथा॥

The woman with attachment to a paramour cannot fully do the work as a woman attached to her domestic duties does, with enthusiasm.

Chapter 9 · Verse 87

9.87

एवं ध्यानैकनिष्ठोऽपि लेशाल्लौकिकमाचरेत्। तत्त्ववित्त्वविरोधित्वाल्लौकिकं सम्यगाचरेत्॥

Similarly, a man who practises meditation one-pointedly, indifferently performs his worldly affairs; but a man who has realised the truth fulfils his worldly duties well, as they do not come in conflict with his knowledge.

Chapter 9 · Verse 88

9.88

मायामयः प्रपञ्चोऽयमात्मा चैतन्यरूपधृक्। इति बोधे विरोधः को लौकिकव्यवहारिणः॥

This world is illusory, Māyā and the Self is by nature pure consciousness. How can such knowledge be opposed to his worldly activities?

Chapter 9 · Verse 89

9.89

अपेक्षते व्यवहृतिर्न प्रपञ्चस्य वस्तुताम्। नाप्यात्मजाड्यं किंत्वेषा साधनान्येव काङ्क्षति॥

To perform activities, the world need not be thought real nor Self as insentient matter. To do so the right means only are necessary.

Chapter 9 · Verse 90

9.90

मनोवाक्कायतद्बाह्यपदार्थाः साधनानि तान्। तत्त्वविन्नोपमृद्नाति व्यवहारोऽस्य नो कुतः॥

These means are the mind, the speech, body and external objects. They do not disappear on enlightenment. So why can’t he engage himself in worldly affairs?

Chapter 9 · Verse 91

9.91

उपमृद्नाति चित्तं चेद्ध्यातासौ न तु तत्त्ववित्। न बुद्धिं मर्द्दयन्दृष्टो घटतत्त्वस्य वेदिता॥

If he controls and concentrates his mind, he is a meditator and not a knower of truth. To know a pot the mind need not be controlled.

Chapter 9 · Verse 92

9.92

सकृत्प्रत्ययमात्रेण घटश्चेद्भासते तदा। स्वप्रकाशोऽयमात्मा किं घटवच्च न भासते॥

(Doubt): A pot once known by a modification of intellect, Vṛtti, remains so always. (Reply): Is not the self-illumined Self also ever manifest?

Chapter 9 · Verse 93

9.93

स्वप्रकाशतया किं ते तद्बुद्धिस्तत्त्ववेदनम्। बुद्धिश्च क्षणनाश्येति चोद्यं तुल्यं घटादिषु॥

(Doubt): Does the self-luminous property of the Self give you the knowledge of Brahman? The Vṛtti with Brahman as the object is the cognition of truth, but the Vṛtti perishes in a moment. (Reply): This objection also applies to the cognition of a pot.

Chapter 9 · Verse 94

9.94

घटादौ निश्चिते बुद्धिर्नश्यत्येव यदा घटः। इष्टो नेतुं तदा शक्य इति चेत्सममात्मनि॥

(Doubt): Once an intellectual conviction of the pot’s existence is established, the cognition (Vṛtti) of the pot perishes. Afterwards it can be recognised at the will of the cogniser. (Reply): The same applies to the cognition of the Self.

Chapter 9 · Verse 95

9.95

निश्चित्य सकृदात्मानं यदापेक्षा तदैव तत्। वक्तुं मन्तुं तथा ध्यातुं शक्नोत्येव हि तत्त्ववित्॥

Once the nature of the Self has been conclusively determined, the knower can speak of it, think of it or meditate on it at will.

Chapter 9 · Verse 96

9.96

उपासक इव ध्यायं लौकिकं विस्मरेत् यदि। विस्मरत्येव सा ध्यानाद्विस्मृतिर्न तु वेदनात्॥

(Doubt): The knower too, like a meditator, forgets worldly affairs in his contemplation. (Reply): Let him forget. This forgetfulness is due to his meditation and not because of his knowledge of the Self.

Chapter 9 · Verse 97

9.97

ध्यानं त्वैच्छिकमेतस्य वेदनान्मुक्तिसिद्धितः। ज्ञानादेव तु कैवल्यमिति शास्त्रेषु डिण्डिमः॥

Meditation is left to his will, for his release has been achieved through knowledge. From knowledge alone comes release. This the scriptures announce with drum-beats.

Chapter 9 · Verse 98

9.98

तत्त्वविद्यदि न ध्यायेत्प्रवर्तेत तदा बहिः। प्रवर्ततां सुखेनायं को बाधोऽस्य प्रवर्तने॥

(Doubt): If a knower does not meditate, he would be drawn to external affairs. (Reply): Let him happily engage himself in them. What is the objection for a knower to be so engaged?

Chapter 9 · Verse 99

9.99

अतिप्रसङ्ग इति चेत्प्रसङ्गं तावदीरय। प्रसङ्गो विधिशास्त्रं चेन्न तत्तत्त्वविदं प्रति॥

(Doubt): This sort of reasoning is wrong, for there the scriptures will be violated. (Reply): If so, what is right reasoning please? (Doubt): Right reasoning is to follow the injunctions and prohibitions of the scriptures. (Reply): But they do not apply to the enlightened.

Chapter 9 · Verse 100

9.100

वर्णाश्रमवयोवस्थाभिमानो यस्य विद्यते। तस्यैव हि निषेधाश्च विधयः सकला अपि॥

All these injunctions and prohibitions are meant for those who believe themselves to belong to a certain caste or station and stage of life.

Chapter 9 · Verse 101

9.101

वर्णाश्रमादयो देहे मायया परिकल्पिताः। नात्मनो बोधरूपस्येत्येवं तस्य विनिश्चयः॥

The knower is convinced that caste, station etc., are creations of Māyā and that they refer to the body and not to the Self whose nature is pure consciousness.

Chapter 9 · Verse 102

9.102

समाधिमथ कर्माणि मा करोतु करोतु वा। हृदयेनास्तसर्वास्थो मुक्त एवोत्तमाशयः॥

The clear-sighted knower from whose heart all attachment has vanished is a liberated soul whether he performs or not concentration or action.

Chapter 9 · Verse 103

9.103

नैष्कर्म्येण न तस्यार्थस्तस्यार्थोऽस्ति न कर्मभिः। न समाधानजप्याभ्यां यस्य निर्वासनं मनः॥

He whose mind is free from all desires or former impressions has nothing to gain from either action or inaction, meditation (Samādhi) or repetitions of holy formulas.

Chapter 9 · Verse 104

9.104

आत्मासङ्गस्ततोऽन्यत्स्यादिन्द्रजालं हि मायिकम्। इत्यचञ्चलनिर्णिते कुतो मनसि वासना॥

The Self is associationless and everything other than the Self is a display of the magic of Māyā. When a mind has such a firm conviction, wherefrom will any desire or impression come in it?

Chapter 9 · Verse 105

9.105

एवं नास्ति प्रसङ्गोऽपि कुतोऽस्यातिप्रसञ्जनम्। प्रसङ्गो यस्य तस्यैव शङ्क्येतातिप्रसञ्जनम्॥

Thus when for an illumined sage there is no injunction on prohibition, where is his violating them? Only for him can violation be possible who is bound by them.

Chapter 9 · Verse 106

9.106

विध्यभावान्न बालस्य दृश्यतेऽतिप्रसञ्जनम्। स्यात्कुतोऽतिप्रसङ्गोऽस्य विध्यभावे समे सति॥

As a child is not subject to any injunctions and prohibitions, he cannot be charged with their violation. In their absence, in the case of a man of realisation too, how can there be any violation?

Chapter 9 · Verse 107

9.107

न किंचिद्वेत्ति बालश्चेत्सर्वं वेत्त्येव तत्त्ववित्। अल्पज्ञस्यैव विधयः सर्वे स्युर्नान्ययोर्द्वयोः॥

(Doubt): But a boy does not know anything. (Reply): A knower of truth knows everything. The law applies to one who knows a little, not to the other two.

Chapter 9 · Verse 108

9.108

शापानुग्रहसामर्थ्यं यस्यासौ तत्त्वविद्यदि। न तत् शापादिसामर्थ्यं फलं स्यात्तपसो यतः॥

(Doubt): He is a knower of truth who can bless or curse with effect. (Reply): Not that, for these powers result from the practice of austerities.

Chapter 9 · Verse 109

9.109

व्यासादेरपि सामर्थ्यं दृश्यते तपसो बलात्। शापादिकारणादन्यत्तपोज्ञानस्य कारणम्॥

(Doubt): Vyāsa and others had these powers. (Reply): But these were produced by some austerities. Austerities meant for knowledge are different from them.

Chapter 9 · Verse 110

9.110

द्वयं यस्यास्ति तस्यैव सामर्थ्यज्ञानयोर्जनिः। एकैकं तु तपः कुर्वन्नेकैकं लभते फलम्॥

Those who practise both the types of austerities possess both powers and knowledge. So each type of practice will produce the result appropriate to it.

Chapter 9 · Verse 111

9.111

सामर्थ्यहीनो निन्द्यश्चेद्यतिभिर्विधिवर्जितः। निन्द्यन्ते यतयोऽप्यन्यैरनिशं भोगलंपटैः॥

(Doubt): Ascetics and ritualists, despise the saintly monk who has neither such powers nor follow the injunctions. (Reply): Their austerities and rituals are also despised by the votaries of worldly pleasures.

Chapter 9 · Verse 112

9.112

भिक्षावस्त्रादि रक्षेयुर्यद्येते भोगतुष्टये। अहो यतित्वमेतेषां वैराग्यभरमन्थरम्॥

(Doubt): Monks too find a pleasure in the acquisition of alms, clothes and shelter. (Reply): Then what wonderful renunciation they must have being unable to move as it were with their dispassion!

Chapter 9 · Verse 113

9.113

वर्णाश्रमपरान्मूर्खा निन्दन्त्वित्युच्यते यदि। देहात्ममतयो बुद्धं निन्दन्त्वाश्रममानिनः॥

(Doubt): It does not matter if the ritualists observing the scriptural rules are abused by the ignorant. (Reply): It also does not matter if a man of realisation is abused by the ritualists who identify themselves with the body and so observe the rules.

Chapter 9 · Verse 114

9.114

तदित्थं तत्त्वविज्ञाने साधनानुपमर्दनात्। ज्ञानिनाचरितुं शक्यं सम्यग्राज्यादि लौकिकम्॥

Therefore as knowledge of truth does not affect the means, such as the mind and so forth, a man of realisation is able to do worldly activities such as ruling a country.

Chapter 9 · Verse 115

9.115

मिथ्यात्वबुद्ध्या तत्रेच्छा नास्ति चेत्तर्हि मास्तु तत्। ध्यायन्वाथ व्यवहरन्यथारब्धं वसत्वयम्॥

(Doubt): He may not have any desire for worldly affairs since he is convinced of the unreality of the empirical world. (Reply): Let it be; let him be engaged in meditation or work according to his fructifying Karma.

Chapter 9 · Verse 116

9.116

उपासकस्तु सततं ध्यायन्नेव वसेदिति। ध्यानेनैव कृतं तस्य ब्रह्मत्वं विष्णुतादिवत्॥

On the other hand, a meditator should always engage himself in meditation, for through meditation his feeling of identity with Brahman arises, as a devotee has it by meditating on Viṣṇu.

Chapter 9 · Verse 117

9.117

ध्यानोपादानकं यत्तद्ध्यानाभावे विलीयते। वास्तवी ब्रह्मता नैव ज्ञानाभावे विलीयते॥

The feeling of identity, which is the effect of meditation, ceases when the practice is given up; but the true Brahmanhood does not vanish even in the absence of knowledge.

Chapter 9 · Verse 118

9.118

ततोऽभिज्ञापकं ज्ञानं न नित्यं जनयत्यदः। ज्ञापकाभावमात्रेण न हि सत्यं विलीयते॥

The eternal Brahmanhood is revealed by knowledge and not created by it, for even in the absence of the revealer the real entity does not cease to exist.

Chapter 9 · Verse 119

9.119

अस्त्येव उपासकस्यापि वास्तवी ब्रह्मतेति चेत्। पामराणां तिरश्चां च वास्तवी ब्रह्मता न किम्॥

(Doubt): But the Brahmanhood of a meditator also is real. (Reply): True, is not the Brahmanhood of the ignorant and the lower creatures also real?

Chapter 9 · Verse 120

9.120

अज्ञानादपुमर्थत्वमुभयत्रापि तत्समम्। उपवासाद्यथा भिक्षा वरं ध्यानं तथान्यथः॥

Since nescience is common, they do not realise the purpose of their life. But just as begging is better than starving, so also it is better to practise devotion and meditation than to engage in other pursuits.

Chapter 9 · Verse 121

9.121

पामराणां व्यवहृतेर्वरं कर्माद्यनुष्ठितिः। ततोऽपि सगुणोपास्तिर्निर्गुणोपासनं ततः॥

It is better to perform the works ordained in the scriptures than be engrossed in worldly affairs. Better than this is to worship a personal deity and meditation on the attributeless Brahman is still better.

Chapter 9 · Verse 122

9.122

यावद्विज्ञानसामीप्यं तावच्छ्रैष्ठ्यं विवर्धते। ब्रह्मज्ञानाय ते साक्षान्निर्गुणोपासनं शनैः॥

That which is nearer to the realisation of Brahman is superior; and meditation on the Absolute gradually becomes like direct realisation of Brahman.

Chapter 9 · Verse 123

9.123

यथा संवादिविभ्रान्तिः फलकाले प्रमायते। विद्यायते तथोपास्तिर्मुक्तिकालेऽतिपाकतः॥

A ‘leading’ error leads to the desired goal, when it becomes knowledge. Similarly meditation on Brahman when ripened, leads to release and becomes real knowledge.

Chapter 9 · Verse 124

9.124

संवादिभ्रमतः पुंसः प्रवृत्तस्यान्यमानतः। प्रमेति चेत्तथोपास्तिर्मान्तरे कारणायताम्॥

(Doubt): A man working prompted by a ‘leading’ error gets correct knowledge not by the leading error but by another evidence. (Reply): The meditation on the Absolute may also be taken as the cause of other evidence (Nididhyāsana leading to direct realisation).

Chapter 9 · Verse 125

9.125

मूर्तिध्यानस्य मन्त्रादेरपि कारणता यदि। अस्तु नाम तथाप्यत्र प्रत्यासत्तिर्विशिष्यते॥

(Doubt): Meditation on the form of a deity and repetition of a sacred formula also lead to the goal. (Reply): Let it be so; but the speciality of meditation on the Absolute is that it is nearest to the goal of Self-realisation.

Chapter 9 · Verse 126

9.126

निर्गुणोपासनं पक्वं समाधिः स्याच्छनैस्ततः। यः समाधिर्निरोधाख्यः सोऽनायासेन लभ्यते॥

When meditation on the attributeless Brahman is mature it leads to Samādhi. This state of intense concentration at case leads on to the Nirodha state in which the distinction between subject and object is eliminated.

Chapter 9 · Verse 127

9.127

निरोधलाभे पुंसोऽन्तरसङ्गं वस्तु शिष्यते। पुनः पुनर्वासितेऽस्मिन्वाक्याज्जायेत तत्त्वधीः॥

When such complete cessation of mental activity is achieved, only the associationless entity (Ātman) remains in his heart. By ceaseless meditation on It based on the great Sayings, arises the knowledge ‘I am Brahman’.

Chapter 9 · Verse 128

9.128

निर्विकारासङ्गनित्यस्वप्रकाशैकपूर्णताः। बुद्धौ झटिति शास्त्रोक्ता आरोहन्त्यविवादतः॥

There is then a perfect realisation of Brahman as the immutable, associationless, eternal, self-revealed, secondless whole, as indicated in the scriptures.

Chapter 9 · Verse 129

9.129

योगाभ्यासस्त्वेतदर्थोऽमृतबिन्द्वादिषु श्रुतः। एवं च दृष्टद्वारापि हेतुत्वादन्यतो वरम्॥

The Amṛta-bindu and other Upaniṣads recommend Yoga for the same object. It is clear therefore that meditation on the attributeless Brahman is superior to other types of worship.

Chapter 9 · Verse 130

9.130

उपेक्ष्य तत्तीर्थयात्रां जपादीनेव कुर्वताम्। पिण्डं समुत्सृज्य करं लेढीति न्याय आपतेत्॥

Those who give up meditation on the attributeless Brahman and undertake pilgrimages, recitations of the holy formulas and other methods, may be compared to ‘those who drop the sweets and lick the hand’.

Chapter 9 · Verse 131

9.131

उपासकानामप्येवं विचारत्यागतो यदि। बाधं तस्माद्विचारस्यासम्भवे योग ईरितः॥

(Doubt): This applies also to those who meditate on the attributeless Brahman giving up enquiry into Its nature. (Reply): True, therefore only those who are not able to practise enquiry have been asked to meditate on the attributeless Brahman.

Chapter 9 · Verse 132

9.132

बहुव्याकुलचित्तानां विचारात्तत्त्वधीर्न हि। योगो मुख्यस्ततस्तेषां धीदर्पस्तेन नश्यति॥

Those who are very fickle-minded and agitated do not have the knowledge of Brahman by the practice of enquiry. Therefore control of the mind is the chief means for them. By it their mind becomes free from distractions.

Chapter 9 · Verse 133

9.133

अव्याकुलधियां मोहमात्रेणाच्छादितात्मनाम्। साङ्ख्यनामा विचाराः स्यान्मुख्यो झटिति सिद्धितः॥

For those whose intellects are no longer distracted nor restless but are merely covered by a veil of ignorance, the analytical system called Sāṅkhya (intellectual enquiry) is prescribed. It will quickly lead them to spiritual illumination.

Chapter 9 · Verse 134

9.134

यत्साङ्ख्यैः प्राप्यते स्थानं तद्योगैरपि गम्यते। एकं साङ्ख्यं च योगं च यः पश्यति स पश्यति॥

‘The state of spiritual balance is obtainable by both the Sāṅkhyas (those who follow the path of enquiry) and the Yogīs (those who practise meditation). He really knows the meaning of the scriptures who knows that the paths of enquiry and meditation are the same’.

Chapter 9 · Verse 135

9.135

तत्कारणं साङ्ख्ययोगाधिगम्यमिति हि श्रुतिः। यस्तु श्रुतेर्विरुद्धः स आभासः साङ्ख्ययोगयोः॥

The Śruti too declares that with both enquiry and meditation people know the Highest; but whatever in the books of Sāṅkhya and Yoga are against the Śruti are to be rejected.

Chapter 9 · Verse 136

9.136

उपासनं नातिपक्वमिह यस्य परत्र सः। मरणे ब्रह्मलोके वा तत्त्वं विज्ञाय मुच्यते॥

If one fails to perfect the practice of meditation in this life, one does so either at the time of death or in the region of Brahmā. Then, obtaining direct knowledge of the reality, one is liberated.

Chapter 9 · Verse 137

9.137

यं यं चापि स्मरन्भावं त्यजत्यन्ते कलेवरम्। तं तमेवैति यच्चित्तस्तेन यातीति शास्त्रतः॥

The Gītā says that a man attains that which he thinks of at the time of death. Wherever his mind is fixed, there he goes, says the Śruti too.

Chapter 9 · Verse 138

9.138

अन्त्यप्रत्ययतो नूनं भाविजन्म तथा सति। निर्गुणप्रत्ययोऽपि स्यात्सगुणोपासने यथा॥

So the future life of a man is determined by the nature of his thoughts at the time of death. Then as a devotee of the Personal God is absorbed in Him, so a meditator on the attributeless Brahman is absorbed in It and obtains Liberation.

Chapter 9 · Verse 139

9.139

नित्यं निर्गुणरूपं तन्नाममात्रेण गीयताम्। अर्थतोमोक्ष एवैष संवादि भ्रमवन्मतः॥

Brahman is called ‘eternal’ and ‘attributeless’ but in fact It is of the nature of liberation itself, just as ‘leading’ error is an error in name only, for it leads to the desired object.

Chapter 9 · Verse 140

9.140

तत्सामर्थ्याज्जायते धीर्मूलाविद्यानिवर्तिका। अविमुक्तोपासनेन तारकब्रह्म बुद्धिवत्॥

As by meditation on the Personal God knowledge of the nature of Īśvara arises, so by meditation on the attributeless Brahman, knowledge of Its nature arises and destroys the ignorance which is the root of rebirth.

Chapter 9 · Verse 141

9.141

सकामो निष्काम इति ह्यशरीरो निरिन्द्रियः। अभयं हीति मुक्तत्वं तापनीये फलं श्रुतम्॥

A meditator becomes Brahman who is ‘unattached, desireless, free from body and organs and fearless’. Thus the Tāpanīya Upaniṣad speaks of liberation as the result of meditation on the attributeless Brahman.

Chapter 9 · Verse 142

9.142

उपासनस्य सामर्थ्याद्विद्योत्पत्तिर्भवेत्ततः। नान्यः पन्था इति ह्येतच्छास्त्रं नैव विरुध्यते॥

By the strength of meditation on the attributeless Brahman knowledge arises. So the scriptural verse, ‘Verily there is no other path to liberation (except knowledge)’ does not conflict with this.

Chapter 9 · Verse 143

9.143

निष्कामोपासनान्मुक्तिस्तापनीये समीरिता। ब्रह्मलोकः सकामस्य शैब्यप्रश्ने समीरितः॥

So the Tāpanīya Upaniṣad points out that liberation comes from desireless meditation. The Praśna Upaniṣad also says that by meditation with desire one enters into the region of Brahmā.

Chapter 9 · Verse 144

9.144

य उपास्ते त्रिमात्रेण ब्रह्मलोके स नीयते। स एतस्माज्जीवघनात्परं पुरुषमीक्षते॥

The Praśna Upaniṣad says that he who meditates with desires on the three-lettered ‘Aum (= Om)’, is taken to the region of Brahmā. There he comes to know the attributeless Brahman who is beyond Hiraṇya-garbha, the sum total of souls and becomes free.

Chapter 9 · Verse 145

9.145

अप्रतीकाधिकरणे तत्क्रतुर्न्याय ईरितः। ब्रह्मलोकफलं तस्मात्सकामस्येति वर्णितम्॥

The Brahma Sūtras in the Apratikādhikaraṇa say that he who desires the region of Brahmā and meditates with desires on the attributeless Brahman attains that region.

Chapter 9 · Verse 146

9.146

निर्गुणोपास्तिसामर्थ्यात्तत्र तत्त्वमवेक्षणत्। पुनरावर्तते नायं कल्पान्ते तु विमुच्यते॥

Such a worshipper, by virtue of his meditation on the attributeless Brahman, enters the world of Brahmā and there obtains direct knowledge of Brahman. He is not born again, he gets ultimate release at the end of the four Yugas.

Chapter 9 · Verse 147

9.147

प्रणवोपास्तयः प्रायो निर्गुणा एव वेदगाः। क्वचित्सगुणता प्रोक्ता प्रणवोपासनस्य हि॥

In the Vedas meditation on the holy syllable Om in most places means meditation on the attributeless Brahman, though in some places it means meditation on Brahman with attributes.

Chapter 9 · Verse 148

9.148

परापरब्रह्मरूप ओङ्कार उपवर्णितः। पिप्पलादेन मुनिना सत्यकामाय पृच्छते॥

Pippalāda being asked by his pupil Satya-kāma says that Om means Brahman both with and without attributes.

Chapter 9 · Verse 149

9.149

एतदालम्बनं ज्ञात्वा यो यदिच्छति तस्य तत्। इति प्रोक्तं यमेनापि पृच्छते नचिकेतसे॥

Yama too, questioned by his pupil Naciketas, replied that he who meditates on Om knowing it as the attributeless Brahman obtains the fulfilment of his desires.

Chapter 9 · Verse 150

9.150

इह वा मरणे वास्य ब्रह्मलोकेऽथवा भवेत्। ब्रह्मसाक्षात्कृतिः सम्यगुपासीनस्य निर्गुणम्॥

He who meditates properly on the attributeless Brahman gets direct knowledge of Brahman either in this life or at the time of death or in the world of Brahmā.

Chapter 9 · Verse 151

9.151

अर्थोऽयमात्मगीतायामपि स्पष्टमुदीरितः। विचाराक्षम आत्मानमुपासीतेति सन्ततम्॥

The Ātmā Gītā also clearly says that those who cannot practise discrimination should always meditate on the Self.

Chapter 9 · Verse 152

9.152

साक्षात्कर्तुमशक्तोऽपि चिन्तयेन्मामशङ्कितः। कालेनानुभवारूढो भवेयं फलतो ध्रुवम्॥

(The Self as if says): ‘Even if direct knowledge of Me does not seem to be possible, a man should still meditate on the Self. In the course of time, he doubtlessly realises the Self and is freed’.

Chapter 9 · Verse 153

9.153

यथागाधनिधेःलब्धौ नोपायः खननं विना। मल्लभेऽपि तथा स्वात्मचिन्तां मुक्ता न चापरः॥

‘To reach treasures deeply hidden in the earth, there is nothing for it but to dig. So to have direct knowledge of Me, the Self, there is no other means than meditation on one’s Self’.

Chapter 9 · Verse 154

9.154

देहोपलमपाकृत्य बुद्धिकुद्दलकात्पुनः। खात्वा मनोभुवं भूयो गृह्णीयान्मां निधिं पुमान्॥

‘A man should remove the stones of body consciousness from the field of the mind and then by repeatedly digging with the pick-axe, the intellect, he can get the hidden treasure of the Self.’

Chapter 9 · Verse 155

9.155

अनुभूतेरभावेऽपि ब्रह्मास्मीत्येव चिन्त्यताम्। अप्यसत् प्राप्यते ध्यानान्नित्याप्तं ब्रह्म किं पुनः॥

Even if there is no realisation, think ‘I am Brahman’. Through meditation a man achieves even other things (like the Deities), why not Brahman who is ever-achieved?

Chapter 9 · Verse 156

9.156

अनात्मबुद्धिशैथिल्यं फलं ध्यानाद्दिने दिने। पश्यन्नपि न चेद्ध्यायेत्कोऽपरोऽस्मात् पशुर्वद॥

If a man, who is convinced by his experience that meditation, practised day by day, destroys the idea that the not-Self is the Self, nevertheless becomes idle and neglects meditation, what difference, tell us, is there between him and a brute?

Chapter 9 · Verse 157

9.157

देहाभिमानं विध्वस्य ध्यानादात्मानमद्वयम्। पश्यन्मर्त्यो मृतो भूत्वा ह्यत्र ब्रह्म समश्नुते॥

Destroying his idea that the body is the Self, through meditation a man sees the secondless Self, becomes immortal and realises Brahman in this body itself.

Chapter 9 · Verse 158

9.158

ध्यानदीपमिमं सम्यक्परामृषति यो नरः। मुक्तसंशय एवायं ध्यायति ब्रह्म सन्ततम्॥

The meditator who studies this Chapter called the ‘Lamp of Meditation’, is freed from all his doubts and meditates constantly on Brahman.

Chapter 10

Chapter 10 · Verse 1

10.1

परमात्माद्वयानन्दपूर्णः पूर्वं स्वमायया। स्वयमेव जगद्भूत्वा प्राविशज्जीवरूपतः॥

Before the projection of the world the Supreme Self, the secondless, all-bliss and ever complete, alone existed. Through His Māyā He became the world and entered into it as the Jīva, the individual Self.

Chapter 10 · Verse 2

10.2

देवाद्युत्तमदेहेषु प्रविष्टो देवताभवत्। मर्त्याद्यधमदेहेषु स्थितो भजति देवताम्॥

Entering the superior bodies like that of Viṣṇu, He became the deities; and remaining in the inferior bodies like that of men He worships the deities.

Chapter 10 · Verse 3

10.3

अनेकजन्मभजनात्स्वविचारं चिकीर्षति। विचारेण विनष्टायां मायायां शिष्यते स्वयम्॥

Due to the practice of devotions in many lives the Jīva desires to reflect upon his nature. When by enquiry and reflection Māyā is negated, the Self alone remains.

Chapter 10 · Verse 4

10.4

अद्वयानन्दरूपस्य सद्वयत्वं च दुःखिता। बन्धः प्रोक्तः स्वरूपेण स्थितिर्मुक्तिरितीर्यते॥

The duality and misery of the secondless Self, whose nature is bliss, is called bondage (bandha). Abiding in Its own nature is said to be liberation (mukti).

Chapter 10 · Verse 5

10.5

अविचारकृतो बन्धो विचारेण निवर्तते। तस्माज्जीवपरात्मानौ सर्वदैव विचारयेत्॥

Bondage is caused by want of discrimination and is negated by discrimination. Hence one should discriminate about the individual and supreme Self.

Chapter 10 · Verse 6

10.6

अहमित्यभिमन्ता यः कर्तासौ तस्य साधनम्। मनस्तस्य क्रिये अन्तर्बहिर्वृत्ति क्रमोत्थिते॥

He who thinks ‘I am’ is the agent. Mind is his instrument of action and the actions of the mind are two types of modifications in succession, internal and external.

Chapter 10 · Verse 7

10.7

अन्तर्मुखाहमित्येषा वृत्तिः कर्तारमुल्लिखेत्। बहिर्मुखेदमित्येषा बाह्यं वस्त्विदमुल्लिखेत्॥

The internal modification of the mind takes the form of ‘I’. It makes him an agent. The external modification assumes the form of ‘this’. It reveals to him the external things.

Chapter 10 · Verse 8

10.8

इदमो ये विशेषाः स्युर्गन्धरूपरसादयः। असाङ्कर्येण तान्भिद्याद्घ्राणादीन्द्रियपञ्चकम्॥

The external things (that are cognised by the mind in a general way, their special qualities having been jumbled up) are cognised by the five sense-organs quite distinctly as sound, touch, colour, taste and smell.

Chapter 10 · Verse 9

10.9

कर्तारं च क्रियां तद्वद्व्यावृत्तविषयानपि। स्फोरयेदेकयत्नेन योऽसौ साक्ष्यत्र चिद्वपुः॥

That consciousness which reveals at one and the same time the agent, the action and the external objects is called ‘witness’ in the Vedānta.

Chapter 10 · Verse 10

10.10

ईक्षे शृणोमि जिघ्रामि स्वादयामि स्पृशाम्यहम्। इति भासयते सर्वं नृत्यशालास्थदीपवत्॥

The witness, like the lamp in a dancing hall, reveals all these as ‘I see’, ‘I hear’, ‘I smell’, ‘I taste’, ‘I touch’ as pieces of knowledge.

Chapter 10 · Verse 11

10.11

नृत्यशालास्थितो दीपः प्रभुं सभ्यांश्च नर्तकीम्। दीपयेदविशेषेण तदभावेऽपि दीप्यते॥

The light in the dancing hall uniformly reveals the patron, the audience and the dancer. Even when they are absent, the light continues to shine.

Chapter 10 · Verse 12

10.12

अहङ्कारं धियं साक्षी विषयानपि भासयेत्। अहङ्काराद्यभावेऽपि स्वयं भात्येव पूर्ववत्॥

The witness-consciousness lights up the ego, the intellect and the sense-objects. Even when ego etc., are absent, it remains self-luminous as ever.

Chapter 10 · Verse 13

10.13

निरन्तरं भासमाने कूटस्थे ज्ञप्तिरूपतः। तद्भासा भास्यमानेयं बुद्धिर्नृत्यत्यनेकधा॥

The unchangeable witness is ever present as self-luminous consciousness; the intellect functions under its light and dances in a variety of ways.

Chapter 10 · Verse 14

10.14

अहङ्कारः प्रभुः सभ्या विषया नर्तकी मतिः। तालादिधारिण्यक्षाणि दीपः साक्ष्यवभासकः॥

In this illustration the patron is the ego, the various sense-objects are the audience, the intellect is the dancer, the musicians playing on their instruments are the sense-organs and the light illumining them all is the witness-consciousness.

Chapter 10 · Verse 15

10.15

स्वस्थानसंस्थितो दीपः सर्वतो भासयेद्यथा। स्थिरस्थायी तथा साक्षी बहिरन्तः प्रकाशयेत्॥

As the light reveals all the objects remaining in its own place, so the witness-consciousness, itself ever motionless, illumines the objects within and without (including the operations of the mind).

Chapter 10 · Verse 16

10.16

बहिरन्तर्विभागोऽयं देहापेक्षो न साक्षिणि। विषया बाह्यदेशस्था देहस्यान्तरहङ्कृतिः॥

The distinction between external and internal objects refers to the body and not to the witness-consciousness. Sense-objects are outside the body whereas the ego is within the body.

Chapter 10 · Verse 17

10.17

अन्तस्था धीः सहैवाक्षैर्बहिर्याति पुनः पुनः। भास्यबुद्धिस्थचाञ्चल्यं साक्षिण्यारोप्यते वृथा॥

The mind seated within goes out again with the sense organs. In vain, people seek to impose the fickleness of the mind illumined by the witness-consciousness on the latter.

Chapter 10 · Verse 18

10.18

गृहान्तरगतः स्वल्पो गवाक्षादातपोऽचलः। तत्र हस्ते नर्त्यमाने नृत्यतीवातपो यथा॥

The streak of sunlight coming into the room through an opening is motionless; but, if one dances one’s hand in the rays, the light appears to be dancing.

Chapter 10 · Verse 19

10.19

निजस्थानस्थितः साक्षी बहिरन्तर्गमागमौ। अकुर्वन्बुद्धिचाञ्चल्यात्करोतीव तथा तथा॥

Similarly, the witness-consciousness, though really fixed in its own place and neither going out nor returning within, yet appears to move owing to the restless nature of the mind.

Chapter 10 · Verse 20

10.20

न बाह्यो नान्तरः साक्षी बुद्धेर्देशौ हि तावुभौ। बुद्ध्याद्यशेषसंशान्तौ यत्र भात्यस्ति तत्र सः॥

The witness-consciousness can neither be called external nor internal. Both these terms have reference to the mind. When the mind becomes fully tranquil, the witness exists where it shines.

Chapter 10 · Verse 21

10.21

देशः कोऽपि न भासेत यदि तर्ह्यस्त्वदेशभाक्। सर्वदेशप्रक्लृप्त्यैव सर्वगत्वं न तु स्वतः॥

If it be said that (when all mental operations cease) there is no space at all, we reply: let it have no space. It is called all-pervasive, because of the mind’s creation of space.

Chapter 10 · Verse 22

10.22

अन्तर्बहिर्वा सर्वं वा यं देशं परिकल्पयेत् । बुद्धिस्तद्देशगः साक्षी तथा वस्तुषु योजयेत् ॥

Whatever space, internal or external, the intellect imagines, is pervaded by the witness-consciousness. Similarly will the witness-consciousness be related to all other objects.

Chapter 10 · Verse 23

10.23

यद्यद्रूपमादौ कल्प्येत बुद्ध्या तत्तत्प्रकाशयन् । तस्य तस्य भवेत्साक्षी स्वतो वाग्बुद्ध्यगोचरः ॥

Whatever form the intellect imagines, the supreme Self illumines it as its witness, remaining Itself beyond the grasp of speech and mind.

Chapter 10 · Verse 24

10.24

कथं तादृङ्मया ग्राह्यमिति चेन्मैव गृह्यताम्। सर्वग्रहोपसंशान्तौ स्वयमेवावशिष्यते॥

If you object ‘How such a Self could be grasped by me?’, our answer is: Let it not be grasped. When the duality of the knower and the known comes to an end, what remains is the Self.

Chapter 10 · Verse 25

10.25

न तत्र मानापेक्षास्ति स्वप्रकाशस्वरूपतः। तादृग्व्युत्पत्त्यपेक्षा चेच्छ्रुतिं पठ गुरोर्मुखात्॥

Since Ātman is self-luminous in its nature, its existence needs no proof. If you need to be convinced that the existence of Ātman needs no proof, hear the instruction of the Śruti from a spiritual teacher.

Chapter 10 · Verse 26

10.26

यदि सर्वगृहत्यागोऽशक्यस्तर्हि धियं व्रज। शरणं तदधीनोऽन्तर्बहिर्वैषोऽनुभूयताम्॥

If you find the renunciation of all perceptible duality impossible, reflect on the intellect and realise the witness-consciousness as the one witness of all internal and external creations of the intellect.

Chapter 11

Chapter 11 · Verse 1

11.1

ब्रह्मानन्दं प्रवक्ष्यामि ज्ञाते तस्मिन्नशेषतः। ऐहिकामुष्मिकानर्थव्रातं हित्वा सुखायते॥

We now describe the bliss of Brahman, knowing which one becomes free from present and future ills and obtains happiness.

Chapter 11 · Verse 2

11.2

ब्रह्मवित्परमाप्नोति शोकं तरति चात्मवित्। रसो ब्रह्मरसं लब्ध्वानन्दी भवति नान्यथा॥

‘A knower of Brahman achieves the Supreme’; ‘A knower of the Self goes beyond sorrow’; ‘Brahman is bliss’; ‘One becomes blissful through the attainment of the blissful Brahman’ and in no other way.

Chapter 11 · Verse 3

11.3

प्रतिष्ठां विन्दते स्वस्मिन्यदा स्यादथ सोऽभयः। कुरुतेऽस्मिन्नन्तरं चेदथ तस्य भयं भवेत्॥

He who establishes himself in his own Self becomes fearless, but he who perceives any difference from the Self is subject to fear.

Chapter 11 · Verse 4

11.4

वायुः सूर्यो वह्निरिन्द्रो मृत्युर्जन्मान्तरेऽन्तरम्। कृत्वा धर्मं विजानन्तोऽप्यस्माद्भीत्या चरन्ति हि॥

Even Wind, Sun, Fire, Indra and Death, having performed the religious practices in earlier lives, but failing to realise their identity with Him, carry out their tasks in fear of Him.

Chapter 11 · Verse 5

11.5

आनन्दं ब्रह्मणो विद्वान्न बिभेति कुतश्चन। एतमेव तपेन्नैषा चिन्ता कर्माग्निसम्भृता॥

One who has attained the bliss of Brahman experiences fear from nothing. Anxiety regarding his good and bad actions which consumes others like fire, no longer scorches him.

Chapter 11 · Verse 6

11.6

एवं विद्वान्कर्मणि द्वे हित्वात्मानं स्मरेत्सदा। कृते च कर्मणि स्वात्मरूपेणैवैष पश्यति॥

Such a knower through his knowledge takes himself beyond good and evil and is ever engaged in meditation on the Self. He looks upon good and bad actions done as the manifestations of his Self.

Chapter 11 · Verse 7

11.7

भिद्यते हृदयग्रन्थिश्च्छिद्यन्ते सर्वसंशयाः। क्षीयन्ते चास्य कर्माणि तस्मिन्दृष्टे परावरे॥

‘When a man has seen the Highest the knots of his heart are sundered; all his doubts are dispelled and all his actions perish’.

Chapter 11 · Verse 8

11.8

तमेव विद्वानत्येति मृत्युं पन्था न चेतरः। ज्ञात्वा देवं पाशहानिः क्षीणैः क्लेशैर्न जन्मभाक्॥

‘Knowing Him, one crosses death; there is no other path than this’. ‘When a man has known the effulgent Self, all his bonds are cut asunder, his afflictions cease; there is no further birth for him.’

Chapter 11 · Verse 9

11.9

देवं मत्वा हर्षशोकौ जहात्यत्रैव धैर्यवान्। नैनं कृताकृते पुण्यपापे तापयतः क्वचित्॥

‘The man of steady wisdom, having known the effulgent Self, leaves behind, even in this life, all joys and sorrows’. ‘He is not scorched by thoughts of the good or bad deeds which he may have done or omitted to do’.

Chapter 11 · Verse 10

11.10

इत्यादिश्रुतयो बह्व्यः पुराणैः स्मृतिभिः सह। ब्रह्मज्ञानेऽनर्थहानिमानन्दं चाप्यघोषयन्॥

Thus many texts in the Śruti, Smṛtis and Purāṇas declare that the knowledge of Brahman destroys all sorrows and leads to bliss.

Chapter 11 · Verse 11

11.11

आनन्दस्त्रिविधो ब्रह्मानन्दो विद्यासुखं तथा। विषयानन्द इत्यादौ ब्रह्मानन्दो विविच्यते॥

Bliss is of three kinds: The bliss of Brahman, the bliss which is born of knowledge and the bliss which is produced by contact with outer objects. First the bliss of Brahman is being described.

Chapter 11 · Verse 12

11.12

भृगुः पुत्रः पितुः श्रुत्वा वरुणाद्ब्रह्मलक्षणम्। अन्नप्राणमनोबुद्धिस्त्यक्त्वानन्दं विजज्ञीवान्॥

Bhṛgu learnt the definition of Brahman from his father Varuṇa and negating the food-sheath, the vital-sheath, the mind-sheath and the intellect-sheath as not being Brahman, he realised Brahman reflected in the bliss-sheath.

Chapter 11 · Verse 13

11.13

आनन्दादेव भूतानि जायन्ते तेन जीवनम्। तेषां लयश्च तत्रातो ब्रह्मानन्दो न संशयः॥

All beings are born of bliss and live by It, pass on to It and are finally reabsorbed in it; there is therefore no doubt that Brahman is bliss.

Chapter 11 · Verse 14

11.14

भूतोत्पत्तेः पुरा भूमा त्रिपुटीद्वैतवर्जनात्। ज्ञातृज्ञानज्ञेयरूपा त्रिपुटी प्रलये हि न॥

Before the creation of beings there was only the infinite and no triad of knower, known and knowing; therefore in dissolution the triad again ceases to exist.

Chapter 11 · Verse 15

11.15

विज्ञानमय उत्पन्नो ज्ञाता ज्ञानं मनोमयः। ज्ञेयाः शब्दादयो नैतत्त्रयमुत्पत्तितः पुरा॥

When created, the intellect-sheath is the knower; the mind-sheath is the field of knowledge; sound etc., are the objects known. Before creation they did not exist.

Chapter 11 · Verse 16

11.16

त्रयाभावे तु निर्द्वैतः पूर्ण एवानुभूयते। समाधिसुप्तिमूर्च्छासु पूर्णः सृष्टेः पुरा तथा॥

In the absence of this triad, the secondless, indivisible Self alone exists. The Self alone existed before the projection of the world. Similarly It exists in the states of Samādhi, deep sleep and swoon.

Chapter 11 · Verse 17

11.17

यो भूमा तत्सुखं नाल्पे सुखं त्रेधा विभेदिनि। सनत्कुमारः प्राहैवं नारदायातिशोकिने॥

The infinite Self alone is bliss; there is no bliss in the finite realm of the triad. This Sanat-kumāra told the grieving Nārada.

Chapter 11 · Verse 18

11.18

सपुराणान्पञ्च वेदान् शास्त्राणि विविधानि च। ज्ञात्वाप्यनात्मवित्त्वेन नारदोऽतिशुशोच ह॥

Even though Nārada was versed in the Vedas, the Purāṇas and the various studies, he was full of grief because of not knowing the Self.

Chapter 11 · Verse 19

11.19

वेदाभ्यासात्पुरा तापत्रयमात्रेण शोकिता। पश्चात्त्वभ्यासविस्मारभङ्गगर्वैश्च शोकिता॥

Before he began the study of the Vedas he was subject to the three usual kinds of misery, but afterwards he was more grieved because of the added afflictions of the practices of the study, the fear of forgetting and slips or defeat and conceit.

Chapter 11 · Verse 20

11.20

सोऽहं विद्वान्प्रशोचामि शोकपारं नयस्व माम्। इत्युक्तः सुखमेवास्य पारमित्यभ्यधादृषिः॥

‘O Sage’, said Nārada to Sanat-kumāra, ‘learned as I am in the studies, I am subject to grief. Please take me beyond this ocean of misery’. The Ṛṣi told Nārada in reply that the farther shore of the ocean of misery is the bliss of Brahman.

Chapter 11 · Verse 21

11.21

सुखं वैषयिकं शोकसहस्रेणावृतत्वतः। दुःखमेवेति मत्वाह नाल्पेऽस्ति सुखमित्यसौ॥

As the happiness derived from sense-objects is covered by thousands of afflictions, it is misery only. There is therefore no happiness in the limited.

Chapter 11 · Verse 22

11.22

ननु द्वैते सुखं माभूदद्वैतेऽप्यस्ति नो सुखम्। अस्ति चेदुपलभ्येत तथा च त्रिपुटी भवेत्॥

(Objection): Granting there is no happiness in duality, there is no happiness in non-duality either. If you maintain that there is, then it must be experienced and then there will be the triad.

Chapter 11 · Verse 23

11.23

मास्त्वद्वैते सुखं किन्तु सुखमद्वैतमेव हि। किं मानमिति चेन्नास्ति मानाकाङ्क्षा स्वयं प्रभे॥

(Reply): ‘Let there be no experience of happiness in the state of non-duality. But non-duality itself is bliss.’ ‘What is the proof?’ ‘The self-revealing requires no other proof’.

Chapter 11 · Verse 24

11.24

स्वप्रभत्वे भवद्वाक्यं मानं यस्माद्भवानिदम्। अद्वैतमभ्युपेत्यास्मिन्सुखं नास्तीति भाषते॥

Your objection itself is evidence of the self-revealing nature of the existence of self-conscious non-duality; for you admit the existence of the secondless and merely contend that it is not bliss.

Chapter 11 · Verse 25

11.25

नाभ्युपैम्यहमद्वैतं त्वद्वचोऽनूद्य दूषणम्। वच्मीति चेत्तदा ब्रूहि किमासीद्द्वैततः पुरा॥

(Objection): I do not admit non-duality but only accept it as a hypothesis to be refuted. (Reply): Then tell us what existed before duality emerged.

Chapter 11 · Verse 26

11.26

किमद्वैतमुत द्वैतमन्यो वा कोटिरन्तिमः। अप्रसिद्धो न द्वितीयोऽनुत्पत्तेः शिष्यतेऽग्रिमः॥

Was it non-duality or duality or something different from both? It cannot have been the last because it is impossible to conceive so. It cannot have been duality because it had not yet emerged. Hence non-duality alone remains.

Chapter 11 · Verse 27

11.27

अद्वैतसिद्धिर्युक्त्यैव नानुभूत्येति चेद्वद। निर्दृष्टान्ता सदृष्टान्ता वा कोट्यन्तरमत्र नो॥

(Objection): The truth of non-duality is established by argument only and not by experience, it cannot be experienced. (Reply): Then tell whether your argument can or cannot be supported by illustration; it must be the one or the other.

Chapter 11 · Verse 28

11.28

नानुभूतिःर्न दृष्टान्त इति युक्तिस्तु शोभते। सदृष्टान्तत्वपक्षे तु दृष्टान्तं वद मे मतम्॥

You deny (the possibility of) the non-dual experience. (At the same time if you say) there is no illustration (in support of the argument that establishes non-duality) it would be a wonderful logic! (You cannot say there is no illustration in its favour, for an argument must be supported by an illustration). In case there are examples please give us an acceptable one.

Chapter 11 · Verse 29

11.29

अद्वैतः प्रलयो द्वैतानुपलम्भेन सुप्तिवत्। इति चेत्सुप्तिरद्वैतेत्यत्र दृष्टान्तमीरय॥

(Objection): (Here is the argument with illustration). In dissolution there is non-duality, since duality is not experienced there, as in deep sleep. (Reply): Please give an illustration to support your affirmation of the absence of duality in deep sleep.

Chapter 11 · Verse 30

11.30

दृष्टान्तः परसुप्तिश्चेदहो ते कौशलं महत्। यः स्वसुप्तिं न वेत्त्यस्य परसुप्तौ तु का कथा॥

(Objection): The sleeping state of some other person may be an illustration. (Reply): You are indeed a clever man; you have no knowledge of your own experience in deep sleep, which you are going to prove by giving the illustration of another’s deep sleep and yet you profess to know that of another.

Chapter 11 · Verse 31

11.31

निश्चेष्टत्वात्परः सुप्तो यथाहमिति चेत्तदा। उदाहर्तुः सुषुप्तेस्ते स्वप्रभत्वं बलाद्भवेत्॥

(Objection): The other person is in deep sleep since he is inactive as in my case. (Reply): Then from the force of your illustration you admit the self-revealing nature of the non-dual truth in your own sleep.

Chapter 11 · Verse 32

11.32

नेन्द्रियाणि न दृष्टान्तस्तथाप्यङ्गीकरोषि ताम्। इदमेव स्वप्रभत्वं यद्भानं साधनैर्विना॥

(How?) There are no sense-organs (for you say you are inactive); there is no illustration (for the illustration adduced by you is inadmissible) and yet there is the non-dual (which you admit); this is what is known as the self-revealing nature of the non-dual. So you are forced to admit it.

Chapter 11 · Verse 33

11.33

स्तामद्वैतस्वप्रभत्वे वद सुप्तौ सुखं कथम्। शृणु दुःखं तदा नास्ति ततस्ते शिष्यते सुखम्॥

(Objection): Admitted that there is the non-dual in deep sleep and that it is self-revealing, what about the bliss you spoke of? (Reply): When all misery is absent, that which remains is bliss.

Chapter 11 · Verse 34

11.34

अन्धः सन्नप्यनन्धः स्याद्विद्धोऽविद्धोऽथ रोग्यपि। अरोगीति श्रुतिः प्राह तच्च सर्वे जना विदुः॥

In deep sleep the blind are not blind, the wounded not wounded and the ill no longer ill, say the scriptures. All people too know this.

Chapter 11 · Verse 35

11.35

न दुःखाभावमात्रेण सुखं लोष्टशिलादिषु। द्वयाभावस्य दृष्टत्वादिति चेद्विषमं वचः॥

(Objection): The absence of misery does not necessarily imply bliss, since objects like stone or clay are not seen to experience either misery or happiness. (Reply): This is a false analogy.

Chapter 11 · Verse 36

11.36

मुखदैन्यप्रकाशाभ्यां परदुःखसुखोहनम्। दैन्याद्यभावतो लोष्टे दुःखाद्यूहो न सम्भवेत्॥

One infers another’s grief or joy from his face, melancholy or smiling, but in clay this inference of grief etc., from such indications is impossible.

Chapter 11 · Verse 37

11.37

स्वकीयसुखदुःखे तु नोहनीये ततस्तयोः। भावो वेद्योऽनुभूत्यैव तदभावोऽपि नान्यतः॥

Our happiness and misery, however, are not to be known by inference; both their presence and absence are directly experienced.

Chapter 11 · Verse 38

11.38

तथा सति सुषुप्तौ च दुःखाभावोऽनुभूतितः। विरोधिदुःखराहित्यात्सुखं निर्विघ्नमिष्यताम्॥

In the same way the absence of all miseries is directly experienced in deep sleep and since they are the opposites to bliss their total absence is unhindered bliss which has to be accepted as our experience.

Chapter 11 · Verse 39

11.39

महत्तरप्रयासेन मृदुशय्यादिसाधनम्। कुतः सम्पाद्यते सुप्तौ सुखं चेत्तत्र नो भवेत्॥

If sleep does not produce an experience of bliss why do people make so much efforts to procure soft beds etc.?

Chapter 11 · Verse 40

11.40

दुःखनाशार्थमेवैतदिति चेद्रोगिणस्तथा। भवत्वरोगिणस्ते तत्सुखायैवेति निश्चिनु॥

(Objection): It is only to remove pain. (Reply): That is true for the sick alone. But since healthy people do so too, it must be to obtain happiness.

Chapter 11 · Verse 41

11.41

तर्हि साधनजन्यत्वात्सुखं वैषयिकं भवेत्। भवत्येवात्र निद्रायाः पूर्वं शय्यासनादिजम्॥

(Objection): Then the happiness in sleep is born of objects due to the bed etc. (Reply): It is true that the happiness before going to sleep is due to these accessories.

Chapter 11 · Verse 42

11.42

निद्रायां तु सुखं यत्तज्जन्यते केन हेतुना। सुखाभिमुखधीरादौ पश्चान्मज्जेत्परे सुखे॥

But the happiness experienced in deep sleep is not obtained from any object. A man may go to sleep expecting to be happy, but before long he experiences a happiness of a higher order.

Chapter 11 · Verse 43

11.43

जाग्रद्व्यापृतिभिः श्रान्तो विश्रम्याथ विरोधिनि। अपनीते स्वस्थचितोऽनुभवेद्विषये सुखम्॥

A man fatigued in the pursuit of worldly affairs lies down and removes the obstacles to happiness. His mind being calm, he enjoys the pleasure of resting in bed.

Chapter 11 · Verse 44

11.44

आत्माभिमुखधीवृत्तौ स्वानन्दः प्रतिबिम्बति। अनुभूयैनमत्रापि त्रिपुट्या श्रान्तिमाप्नुयात्॥

Directing his thoughts towards the Self, he experiences the bliss of the Self reflected in the intellect. But experiencing this, even here he becomes tired of the pleasures derived of the triad (of experiencer, experience and experienced).

Chapter 11 · Verse 45

11.45

तत्श्रमस्यापनुत्यर्थं जीवो धावेत्परात्मनि। तेनैक्यं प्राप्य तत्रत्यो ब्रह्मानन्दः स्वयं भवेत्॥

To remove that weariness the Jīva rushes towards his real Self and becoming united with it experiences the bliss of Brahman in sleep.

Chapter 11 · Verse 46

11.46

दृष्टान्ताः शकुनिः श्येनः कुमारश्च महानृपः। महाब्राह्मण इत्येते सुप्त्यानन्दे श्रुतीरिताः॥

The scriptures give the following examples to illustrate the bliss enjoyed in sleep: the falcon, the eagle, the infant, the great king and the knower of Brahman.

Chapter 11 · Verse 47

11.47

शकुनिः सूत्रबद्धः सन्दिक्षु व्यापृत्य विश्रमम्। अलब्ध्वा बन्धनस्थानं हस्तस्तम्भाद्युपाश्रयेत्॥

Tied to a string, the falcon, flying hither and thither but failing to find a resting place, returns to rest on the wrist of its master or on the post to which it is tied.

Chapter 11 · Verse 48

11.48

जीवोपाधिर्मनस्तद्वद्धर्माधर्मफलाप्तये। स्वप्ने जाग्रति च भ्रान्त्वा क्षीणे कर्मणि लीयते॥

Similarly the mind, which is the instrument of the Jīva, moves on in the dreaming and waking states in order to obtain the fruits of righteous and unrighteous deeds. When the experiencing of these fruits ceases, the mind is absorbed in its cause, undifferentiated ignorance.

Chapter 11 · Verse 49

11.49

श्येनो वेगेन नीडैकलम्पटः शयितुं व्रजेत्। जीवः सुप्त्यै तथा धावेद्ब्रह्मानन्दैकलम्पटः॥

The eagle rushes only to its nest hoping to find rest there. Similarly the Jīva eager only to experience the bliss of Brahman rushes to sleep.

Chapter 11 · Verse 50

11.50

अतिबालस्तनं पीत्वा मृदुशय्यागतो हसन्। रागद्वेषाद्यनुत्पत्तेरानन्दैकस्वभावभाक्॥

A tiny tot having fed at the breast of its mother, lies smiling in a soft bed. Free from desire and aversion it enjoys the bliss of its nature.

Chapter 11 · Verse 51

11.51

महाराजः सार्वभौमः सुतृप्तः सर्वभोगतः। मानुषानन्दसीमानं प्राप्यानन्दैकमूर्तिभाक्॥

A mighty king, sovereign of the world, having obtained all the enjoyments which mark the limits of human happiness to his full contentment, becomes the very personification of bliss.

Chapter 11 · Verse 52

11.52

महाविप्रो ब्रह्मवेदी कृतकृत्यत्वलक्षणाम्। विद्यानन्दस्य परमां काष्ठां प्राप्यावतिष्ठते॥

A great Brāhmaṇa, a knower of Brahman, has extended the bliss of knowledge to its extreme limit; he has achieved all that was to be achieved and sits established in that state.

Chapter 11 · Verse 53

11.53

मुग्धबुद्धातिबुद्धानां लोके सिद्धा सुखात्मता। उदाहृतानामन्ये तु दुःखिनो न सुखात्मकाः॥

These examples of the ignorant, infant, the discriminative king and the wise Brāhmaṇa are of people considered to be happy. Others are subject to misery and are not very happy.

Chapter 11 · Verse 54

11.54

कुमारादिवदेवायं ब्रह्मानन्दैकतत्परः। स्त्रीपरिष्वक्तवद्वेद न बाह्यं नापि चान्तरम्॥

Like the infant and the other two, man passes into deep sleep and enjoys only the bliss of Brahman. In that state he, like a man embraced by his loving wife, is not conscious of anything either internal or external.

Chapter 11 · Verse 55

11.55

बाह्यं रथ्यादिकं वृत्तं गृहकृत्यं यथान्तरम्। तथा जागरणं बाह्यं नाडीस्थः स्वप्न आन्तरः॥

Just as what happens outside in the street may be called external and what is done inside the house internal, so the experiences of the waking state may be called external and the dreams produced inside the mind and the nervous system may be called internal.

Chapter 11 · Verse 56

11.56

पितापि सुप्तावपितेत्यादौ जीवत्ववारणात्। सुप्तौ ब्रह्मैव नो जीव संसारित्वासमीक्षणात्॥

The Śruti says: ‘In sleep even a father is no father’. Then in the absence of all worldly ideas the Jivahood is lost and a state of pure consciousness prevails.

Chapter 11 · Verse 57

11.57

पितृत्वाद्यभिमानो यः सुखदुःखाकरः स हि। तस्मिन्नपगते तीर्णः सर्वान् शोकान्भवत्ययम्॥

One having such notions as ‘I am a father’ experiences joy and grief. When such attachment perishes, he rises beyond all sorrow.

Chapter 11 · Verse 58

11.58

सुषुप्तिकाले सकले विलीने तमसावृतः। सुखरूपमुपैतीति ब्रूते ह्याथर्वणी श्रुतिः॥

A text of the Atharva Veda says: ‘In the state of deep sleep, when all the objects of experience have been absorbed and only darkness (Tamas) prevails, the Jīva enjoys bliss’.

Chapter 11 · Verse 59

11.59

सुखमस्वाप्समत्राहं नैव किंचिदवेदिषम्। इति द्वे तु सुखाज्ञाने परामृशति चोत्तितः॥

A man from deep sleep remembers his happiness and ignorance and says: ‘I was sleeping happily; I knew nothing then’.

Chapter 11 · Verse 60

11.60

परामर्शोऽनुभूतेऽस्तीत्यासीदनुभवस्तदा। चिदात्मत्वत्स्वतो भाति सुखमज्ञानधीस्ततः॥

Recollection presupposes experience. So in sleep there was experience. The bliss experienced in dreamless sleep is revealed by consciousness itself which also reveals the undifferentiated ignorance (Ajñāna) covering bliss in that state.

Chapter 11 · Verse 61

11.61

ब्रह्मविज्ञानमानन्दमिति वाजसनेयिनः। पठन्त्यतः स्वप्रकाशं सुखं ब्रह्मैव नेतरत्॥

The Vāja-saneyins say: ‘Brahman is of the nature of consciousness and bliss’. Therefore the self-luminous bliss is Brahman itself and nothing else.

Chapter 11 · Verse 62

11.62

यदज्ञानं तत्र लीनौ तौ विज्ञानमनोमयौ। तयोर्हि विलयावस्था निद्राज्ञानं च सैव हि॥

The mind and the intellect sheaths are latent in the state called ignorance. Deep sleep is the condition in which these sheaths are latent and it is therefore a state of ignorance.

Chapter 11 · Verse 63

11.63

विलीनघृतवत्पश्चात्स्याद्विज्ञानमयो घनः। विलीनावस्थ आनन्दमयशब्देन कथ्यते॥

Just as melted butter again becomes solid, the two sheaths in the states following deep sleep again become manifest. The state in which the mind and intellect are latent is called the bliss-sheath.

Chapter 11 · Verse 64

11.64

सुप्तिपूर्वक्षणे बुद्धिवृत्तिर्या सुखबिम्बिता। सैव तद्बिम्बसहिता लीनानन्दमयस्ततः॥

The modifications (Vṛtti) of the intellect in which, just before sleep, bliss is reflected becomes latent in the state of deep sleep along with the reflected bliss and is known as the bliss-sheath.

Chapter 11 · Verse 65

11.65

अन्तर्मुखोऽयमानन्दमयो ब्रह्मसुखं तदा। भुङ्क्ते चिद्बिम्बयुक्ताभिरज्ञानोत्पन्नवृत्तिभिः॥

This Vṛtti thus turned within, which is termed the bliss-sheath, enjoys the bliss reflected on it in association with the modifications of ignorance, catching the reflection of consciousness.

Chapter 11 · Verse 66

11.66

अज्ञानवृत्तयः सूक्ष्मा विस्पष्टा बुद्धिवृत्तयः। इति वेदान्तसिद्धान्तपारगाः प्रवदन्ति हि॥

The adepts in Vedānta say that the modifications of ignorance are subtle (sūkṣmā), whereas those of the intellect are gross (vispaṣṭā, manifest).

Chapter 11 · Verse 67

11.67

माण्डुक्यतापनीयादिश्रुतिष्वेतदतिस्फुटम्। आनन्दमयभोक्तृत्वं ब्रह्मानन्दे च भोग्यता॥

This is fully explained in the Māṇḍukya and Tāpanīya Upaniṣads. It is the sheath of bliss which is the enjoyer and it is the bliss of Brahman which is enjoyed.

Chapter 11 · Verse 68

11.68

एकीभूतः सुषुप्तस्थः प्रज्ञानघनतां गतः। आनन्दमय आनन्दभुक्चेतोमयवृत्तिभिः॥

This profusion of bliss (Ānandamayaḥ), having become concentrated into one mass of consciousness in the deep sleep, enjoys the (reflected) bliss of Brahman with the help of modifications (Vṛttis) reflecting a superabundance of consciousness.

Chapter 11 · Verse 69

11.69

विज्ञानमयमुख्यैर्यो रूपैर्युक्तः पुराधुना। स लयेनैकतां प्राप्तो बहुतण्डुलपिष्टवत्॥

The self (Cid-ābhāsa) in the waking and dream states, is connected or associated with various sheaths such as Vijñānamaya and appears as many (i.e., plays various roles). In the deep sleep state, however, they get merged and become latent like a dough of many (powdered) wheat-grains.

Chapter 11 · Verse 70

11.70

प्रज्ञानानि पुरा बुद्धिवृत्तयोऽथ घनोऽभवत्। घनत्वं हिमबिन्दूनामुदग्देशे यथा तथा॥

The modifications of the intellect, which are instruments of cognition, unite and become one in the state of sleep, just as drops of cold water in the Himalayan regions solidify into a mass of ice.

Chapter 11 · Verse 71

11.71

तद्घनत्वं साक्षिभावं दुःखाभावं प्रचक्षते। लौकिकास्तार्किका यावद्दुःखवृत्तिविलोपनात्॥

This witness state of compact consciousness, ordinary people and the logicians say, is characterised by the absence of suffering, because in that state the mental modifications of pain and misery subside.

Chapter 11 · Verse 72

11.72

अज्ञानबिम्बिता चित्स्यान्मुखमानन्दभोजने। भुक्तं ब्रह्मसुखं त्यक्त्वा बहिर्यात्यथ कर्मणा॥

In the enjoyment of the bliss of Brahman in deep sleep, the consciousness reflected in ignorance is the means. Prompted by its Karma, good or bad, the Jīva gives up the enjoyment of bliss and goes out to the waking state.

Chapter 11 · Verse 73

11.73

कर्म जन्मान्तरेऽभूद्यत्तद्योगाद्बुद्ध्यते पुनः। इति कैवल्यशाखायां कर्मजो बोध ईरितः॥

The Kaivalya Upaniṣad says that a Jīva passes from the sleeping to the waking state owing to the effects of the actions of former births. Reawakening thus is a result of actions.

Chapter 11 · Verse 74

11.74

कंचित्कालं प्रबुद्धस्य ब्रह्मानन्दस्य वासना। अनुगच्छेद्यतस्तूष्णीमास्ते निर्विषयः सुखी॥

For a short time after the waking up the impression of the bliss of Brahman enjoyed during sleep continues. For he remains for some time calm and happy, without taking any interest in the enjoyment of external objects.

Chapter 11 · Verse 75

11.75

कर्मभिः प्रेरितः पश्चान्नाना दुःखानि भावयन्। शनैर्विस्मरति ब्रह्मानन्दमेषोऽखिलो जनः॥

Then, impelled by his past actions ready to bear fruits, he begins to think of duties and their implementation entailing sufferings of many kinds and gradually forgets the bliss of Brahman experienced (a few minutes before).

Chapter 11 · Verse 76

11.76

प्रागूर्ध्वमपि निद्रायाः पक्षपातो दिने दिने। ब्रह्मानन्दे नृणां तेन प्राज्ञोऽस्मिन्विवदेत कः॥

Experiencing the bliss of Brahman before and after sleep day after day man develops a predilection for it. How can a man, therefore, doubt it (i.e., the existence of the bliss of Brahman)?

Chapter 11 · Verse 77

11.77

ननु तूष्णीं स्थितौ ब्रह्मानन्दश्चेद्भाति लौकिकाः। अलसाश्चरितार्थाः स्युः शास्त्रेण गुरुणात्र किम्॥

(Objection): Well, if a mere state of quietude were enjoyment of the bliss of Brahman then the lazy and the worldly would achieve the end of their life. What then is the use of the teacher and the scriptures?

Chapter 11 · Verse 78

11.78

बाढं ब्रह्मेति विद्युश्चेत्कृतार्थास्तावतैव ते। गुरुशास्त्रे विनात्यन्तं गम्भीरं ब्रह्म वेत्ति कः॥

(Reply): Your contention would be correct, if he realised that the bliss that he experienced was the bliss of Brahman. But who can know Brahman that is so immensely profound without the help of the teacher and the scripture?

Chapter 11 · Verse 79

11.79

जानाम्यहं त्वदुक्त्याद्य कुतो मे न कृतार्थता। शृण्वत्र त्वादृशं वृत्तं प्राज्ञं मन्यस्य कस्यचित्॥

(Objection): I know what Brahman is from what you yourself have said. Why then am I without the bliss of realisation? (Reply): Listen to the story of a man who like yourself imagined that he was wise.

Chapter 11 · Verse 80

11.80

चतुर्वेदविदे देयमिति शृण्वन्नवोचत। वेदाश्चत्वार इत्येवं वेद्मि मे दीयतां धनम्॥

This man, hearing that a large reward was offered to anyone who knew the four Vedas, said, ‘I know from you that there are four Vedas. So give me the reward’.

Chapter 11 · Verse 81

11.81

साङ्ख्यमेवैष जानाति न तु वेदानशेषतः। यदि तर्हि तमप्येवं नाशेषं ब्रह्म वेत्सि हि॥

(Objection): He knew the number, not the text, of the Vedas fully. (Reply): You too have not known Brahman fully.

Chapter 11 · Verse 82

11.82

अखण्डैकरसानन्दे मायातत्कार्यवर्जिते। अशेषत्वसशेषत्ववार्तावसर एव कः॥

(Objection): Brahman is by nature indivisible and is bliss absolute, untouched by Māyā and its effects. How can you speak of the knowledge of Brahman as complete or incomplete?

Chapter 11 · Verse 83

11.83

शब्दानेव पठस्याहो तेषामर्थं च पश्यसि। शब्दपाठेऽर्थबोधस्ते सम्पाद्यत्वेन शिष्यते॥

(Reply): Do you simply say the word ‘Brahman’ or do you see its meaning? If you know only the word, it remains for you to acquire knowledge of its meaning.

Chapter 11 · Verse 84

11.84

अर्थे व्याकरणाद्बुद्धे साक्षात्कारोऽवशिष्यते। स्यात्कृतार्थत्वधीर्यावत्तावद्गुरुमुपास्व भोः॥

Even if with the help of grammar and so forth you learn its meaning, still realisation remains. Serve your teacher until you have realised Brahman and known that there is nothing further to be known.

Chapter 11 · Verse 85

11.85

आस्तामेतद्यत्र यत्र सुखं स्याद्विषयैर्विना। तत्र सर्वत्र विद्ध्येतां ब्रह्मानन्दस्य वासनाम्॥

Leave the vain argument alone and know that whenever happiness is felt in the absence of objects, that happiness is an impression of the bliss of Brahman.

Chapter 11 · Verse 86

11.86

विषयेष्वपि लब्धेषु तदिच्छोपरमे सति। अन्तर्मुखमनोवृत्तावानन्दः प्रतिबिम्बति॥
