युवा रूपी च विद्यावान्नीरोगो दृढचित्तवान्। सैन्योपेतः सर्वपृथ्वीं वित्तपूर्णां प्रपालयन्॥ सर्वैर्मानुष्यकैर्भोगैः सम्पन्नस्तृप्तभूमिपः। यमानन्दमवाप्नोति ब्रह्मविच्च तमश्नुते॥

Whatever bliss is attained by a satisfied king who is young, handsome, learned, healthy, strong of mind, who has suitable army and rules over the whole world full of wealth and as such is endowed with the totality of all human enjoyments, even that bliss the knower of Brahman achieves.

Chapter 14 · Verse 23

14.23

मर्त्येभोगे द्वयोर्नास्ति कामस्तृप्तिरतः समा। भोगान्निष्कामतैकस्य परस्यापि विवेकतः॥

For both the king and the knower there is no attraction for worldly enjoyment and so their happiness and contentment are comparable. One has desirelessness because of enjoyment, the other because of discrimination.

Chapter 14 · Verse 24

14.24

श्रोत्रियत्वाद्वेदशास्त्रैर्भोग्यदोषानवेक्षते। राजा बृहद्रथो दोषांस्तान्गाथाभिरुदाहरत्॥

The knower of Brahman knows through his knowledge of the Vedic scriptures the defects of the objects of enjoyment. King Bṛhad-ratha gave examples of those defects in some songs.

Chapter 14 · Verse 25

14.25

देहदोषाश्चित्तदोषा भोग्यदोषा अनेकशः। शुना वान्ते पायसे नो कामस्तद्वद्विवेकिनः॥

Thus Bṛhad-ratha described the defects pertaining to the body, the mind and the objects of enjoyment. As no one has liking for porridge vomited by a dog, likewise the man of discrimination also has no liking for the body etc.

Chapter 14 · Verse 26

14.26

निष्कामत्वे समेऽप्यत्र राज्ञः साधन सञ्चये। दुःखमासीद्भाविनाशादितिभीरनुवर्तते॥

Though there is similarity between the king and the knower of Truth in desirelessness, there was misery for the king in accumulating the objects of enjoyment and the fear of losing them in future follows him.

Chapter 14 · Verse 27

14.27

नोभयं श्रोत्रियस्यातस्तदानन्दोऽधिकोऽन्यतः। गन्धर्वानन्द आशास्ति राज्ञो नास्ति विवेकिनः॥

Both these miseries are absent for the knower; so his bliss is more than that of the king. Besides, the king may have desire for the bliss of the Gandharvas, but the knower has none.

Chapter 14 · Verse 28

14.28

अस्मिन्कल्पे मनुष्यः सन्पुण्यपापविशेषतः। गन्धर्वत्वं समापन्नो मर्त्यो गन्धर्व उच्यते॥

One who has become a Gandharva, because of the particular result of his meritorious actions as a man in the present cycle, is called a ‘human Gandharva’.

Chapter 14 · Verse 29

14.29

पूर्वकल्पे कृतात्पुण्यात्कल्पादावेव चेद्भवेत्। गन्धर्वत्वं तादृषोऽत्र देवगन्धर्व उच्यते॥

If one becomes a Gandharva in the very beginning of the cycle, because of his meritorious actions in the earlier cycle, he is called a ‘celestial Gandharva’.

Chapter 14 · Verse 30

14.30

अग्निष्वात्तादयो लोके पितरश्चिरवासिनः। कल्पादावेव देवत्वं गता आजानदेवताः॥

The Agni-svattas and others who dwell for a long time in their region are called the Pitṛs. Those who have achieved the state of deities in the beginning of their cycle are called Ājāna-devatās.

Chapter 14 · Verse 31

14.31

अस्मिन्कल्पेऽश्वमेधादि कर्म कृत्वा महत्पदम्। अवाप्याजानदेवैर्याः पूज्यास्ताः कर्मदेवताः॥

Those who obtain the glorious position and are fit for worship by the Ājāna-devatās by performing the Aśva-medha sacrifice and other good actions, are the Karma-devatās.

Chapter 14 · Verse 32

14.32

यमाग्निमुख्याः देवाः स्युर्जाताविन्द्रबृहस्पती। प्रजापतिर्विराट् प्रोक्तो ब्रह्मा सूत्रात्मनामकः॥

Yama and Agni are foremost among the gods. Indra and Bṛhas-pati are well known (and superior to them). Prajā-pati is mentioned as Virāṭ and Brahmā is called the Sūtrātman or Hiraṇya-garbha.

Chapter 14 · Verse 33

14.33

सार्वभौमादिसूत्रान्ता उत्तरोत्तरकामिनः। अवाङ्मनसगम्योऽयमात्मानन्दस्ततः परः॥

From the king to Brahmā each desires the joy of the one higher than himself; but the bliss of the Self which is beyond the grasp of the mind and the senses, is superior to that of all others.

Chapter 14 · Verse 34

14.34

तैस्तैः काम्येषु सर्वेषु सुखेषु श्रोत्रियो यतः। निस्पृहस्तेन सर्वेषामानन्दाः सन्ति तस्य ते॥

As the knower of the Vedas has no desire for all those coveted pleasures, the bliss of all creatures are his.

Chapter 14 · Verse 35

14.35

सर्वकामाप्तिरेषोक्ता यद्वा साक्षि चिदात्मता। स्वदेहवत्सर्वदेहेष्वपि भोगानवेक्षते॥

This is described as ‘achieving all the desired objects’. Or it may be explained as the witness-consciousness of the knower experiencing the enjoyments of all the bodies, like those through his own body.

Chapter 14 · Verse 36

14.36

अज्ञस्याप्येतदस्त्येव न तु तृप्तिरबोधतः। यो वेद सोऽश्नुते सर्वान्कामानितियब्रवीच्छ्रुतिः॥

(Doubt): Being the witness-consciousness, even the ignorant man has this (universal enjoyment). (Reply): No, being devoid of the knowledge of himself as the witness he does not experience satisfaction. The Śruti says that he who knows the truth achieves all the desired objects.

Chapter 14 · Verse 37

14.37

यद्वा सर्वात्मता स्वस्य साम्ना गायति सर्वदा। अहमन्नं तथान्नादश्चेति सामस्वधीयते॥

Or he enjoys everything because he becomes all, as that famous passage which expresses his all-pervading selfhood sings: ‘I am the food as well as the eater of the food’.

Chapter 14 · Verse 38

14.38

दुःखाभावश्च कामाप्तिरुभे ह्येवं निरूपिते। कृतकृत्यत्वमन्यच्च प्राप्तप्राप्यत्वमीक्ष्यताम्॥

Thus are established the nature of both the absence of misery and the fulfilment of desires (experienced by the knower of the Self). His other experiences, viz., the satisfaction of having done all that was to be done and of having achieved all that was to be achieved may be seen elsewhere.

Chapter 14 · Verse 39

14.39

उभयं तृप्तिदीपे हि सम्यगस्माभिरीरितम्। त एवात्रानुसन्धेयाः श्लोका बुद्धिविशुद्धये॥

Both the topics have properly been dealt with in Chapter 7 on the ‘Lamp of Perfect Satisfaction’. These verses quoted below should be meditated upon for the purification of the mind.

Chapter 14 · Verses 40–41

14.40–41

ऐहिकामुष्मिकव्रातसिद्ध्यै मुक्तेश्च सिद्धये। बहु कृत्यं पुरास्याभूत्तत्सर्वमधुना कृतम्॥ तदेतत्कृतकृत्यत्वं प्रतियोगिपुरःसरम्। अनुसन्दधदेवायमेवं तृप्यति नित्यशः॥

Before realisation one has many duties to perform in order to acquire worldly and celestial advantages and also as an aid to ultimate release; but with the rise of knowledge of Brahman, they are as good as already done, for nothing further remains to be done. The Jīvan-mukta always feels supreme self-satisfaction by constantly keeping in view his former state and present state of freedom from wants and duties.

Chapter 14 · Verse 42

14.42

दुःखिनोऽज्ञाः संसरन्तु कामं पुत्राद्यपेक्षया। परमानन्दपूर्णोऽहं संसरामि किमिच्छया॥

Let the ignorant people of the world perform worldly actions and desire to possess wives, children and wealth. I am full of supreme bliss. For what purpose should I engage myself in worldly concerns?

Chapter 14 · Verse 43

14.43

अनुतिष्ठन्तु कर्माणि परलोकयियासवः। सर्वलोकात्मकः कस्मादनुतिष्ठामि किं कथम्॥

Let those desirous of joy in heaven perform the ordained rituals. I pervade all the worlds. How and wherefore should I undertake such actions?

Chapter 14 · Verse 44

14.44

व्याचक्षतां ते शास्त्राणि वेदानध्यापयन्तु वा। येऽत्राधिकारिणो मे तु नाधिकारोऽक्रियत्वतः॥

Let those who are entitled to it, explain the scriptures or teach the Vedas. I am not so entitled because all my actions have ceased.

Chapter 14 · Verse 45

14.45

निद्राभिक्षे स्नानशौचे नेच्छामि न करोमि च। द्रष्टारश्चेत्कल्पयन्ति किं मे स्यादन्यकल्पनात्॥

I have no desire to sleep or beg for alms, nor do I do so; nor do I perform the acts of bathing or ablution. The onlookers imagine these things in me. What have I to do with their imaginations?

Chapter 14 · Verse 46

14.46

गुञ्जापुञ्जादि दह्येत नान्यारोपितवह्निना। नान्यारोपितसंसारधर्मानेवमहं भजे॥

Seeing a bush of red guñjā berries from a distance one may suppose that there is a fire, but such as imaginary fire does not affect the bush. So the worldly duties and qualities attributed to me by others do not affect me.

Chapter 14 · Verse 47

14.47

शृण्वन्त्वज्ञाततत्त्वास्ते जानन्कस्माच्छृणोम्यहम्। मन्यन्तां संशयापन्ना न मन्येऽहमसंशयः॥

Let those ignorant of the nature of Brahman listen to the teachings of the Vedānta philosophy. I have Self-knowledge. Why again should I listen to them? Those who are in doubt reflect on the nature of Brahman. I have no doubts, so I do not do so.

Chapter 14 · Verse 48

14.48

विपर्यस्तो निदिध्यासेत्किं ध्यानमविपर्ययात्। देहात्मत्वविपर्यासं न कदाचिद्भजाम्यहम्॥

He who is subject to erroneous conviction may practise meditation. I do not confuse the Self for the body. So in the absence of such a delusion why should I meditate?

Chapter 14 · Verse 49

14.49

अहं मनुष्य इत्यादिव्यवहारो विनाप्यमुम्। विपर्यासं चिराभ्यस्तवासनातोऽवकल्पते॥

Even without being subject to this delusion, I behave like a human being through the impressions and habits gathered over a long period.

Chapter 14 · Verse 50

14.50

प्रारब्धकर्मणि क्षीणे व्यवहारो निवर्तते। कर्माक्षये त्वसौ नैव शाम्येद्ध्यानसहस्रतः॥

All worldly dealings will come to an end when the fructifying Karma wears out. If it does not wear out, thousands of meditational bouts will not stop the dealings.

Chapter 14 · Verse 51

14.51

विरलत्वं व्यवहृतेरिष्टं चेद्ध्यानमस्तु ते। अबाधिकां व्यवहृतिं पश्यन्ध्यायाम्यहं कुतः॥

To bring to an end your worldly dealings, you may practise contemplation as much as you like, but I know the worldly dealings to be perfectly harmless. Why should I then meditate?

Chapter 14 · Verse 52

14.52

विक्षेपो नास्ति यस्मान्मे न समाधिस्ततो मम। विक्षेपो वा समाधिर्वा मनसः स्याद्विकारिणः॥

There is no distraction for me, so for me there is no need of Samādhi too. Both distraction and absorption are states of the changeable mind.

Chapter 14 · Verse 53

14.53

नित्यानुभवरूपस्य को मे वाऽनुभवः पृथक्। कृतं कृत्यं प्रापणीयं प्राप्तमित्येव निश्चयः॥

I am the sum of all the experiences in the universe; where is the separate experience for me? I have obtained all that was to be obtained and have done all that was to be done. This is my unshakeable conviction.

Chapter 14 · Verse 54

14.54

व्यवहारो लौकिको वा शास्त्रीयो वाऽन्यथाऽपि वा। ममाकर्तुरलेपस्य यथाऽऽरब्धं प्रवर्तताम्॥

I am associationless, neither the doer nor the enjoyer. I am not concerned with what the past actions make me do, whether in accordance with or against the social or scriptural codes.

Chapter 14 · Verse 55

14.55

अथवा कृतकृत्योऽपि लोकानुग्रहकामया। शास्त्रीयेणैव मार्गेण वर्तेऽहं का मम क्षतिः॥

Or, there is no harm if I engage myself in doing good to the world following the scriptural injunctions even though I have obtained all that was to be obtained.

Chapter 14 · Verse 56

14.56

देवार्चनस्नानशौचभिक्षादौ वर्ततां वपुः। तारं जपतु वाक्तद्वत्पठत्वाम्नायमस्तकम्॥

Let my body worship God, take bath, preserve cleanliness or beg for alms. Let my mind recite ‘Om’ or study the Upaniṣads.

Chapter 14 · Verse 57

14.57

विष्णुं ध्यायतु धीर्यद्वा ब्रह्मानन्दे विलीयताम्। साक्ष्यहं किञ्चिदप्यत्र न कुर्वे नापि कारये॥

Let my intellect meditate on Viṣṇu or be merged in the bliss of Brahman, I am the witness of all. I do nothing nor cause anything to be done.

Chapter 14 · Verse 58

14.58

कृतकृत्यतया तृप्तः प्राप्तप्राप्यतया पुनः। तृप्यन्नेवं स्वमनसा मन्यतेऽसौ निरन्तरम्॥

As he has achieved all that was to be achieved and nothing else remains for him to do, he feels satisfied and always things thus:

Chapter 14 · Verse 59

14.59

धन्योऽहं धन्योऽहं नित्यं स्वात्मानमञ्जसा वेद्मि। धन्योऽहं धन्योऽहं ब्रह्मानन्दो विभाति मे स्पष्टम्॥

Blessed am I (dhanyo’ham), blessed, for I have the constant vision of my Self! Blessed am I, blessed, for the bliss of Brahman shines clearly to me!

Chapter 14 · Verse 60

14.60

धन्योऽहं धन्योऽहं दुःखं सांसारिकं न वीक्षेऽद्य। धन्योऽहं धन्योऽहं स्वस्याज्ञानं पलायितं क्वापि॥

Blessed am I, blessed, for I am free from the sufferings of the world. Blessed am I, blessed, for my ignorance has fled away, I know not where.

Chapter 14 · Verse 61

14.61

धन्योऽहं धन्योऽहं कर्तव्यं मे न विद्यते किञ्चित्। धन्योऽहं धन्योऽहं प्राप्तव्यं सर्वमद्य सम्पन्नम्॥

Blessed am I, blessed, for I have no further duty to perform. Blessed am I, blessed, for I have now achieved the highest that one can aspire to.

Chapter 14 · Verse 62

14.62

धन्योऽहं धन्योऽहं तृप्तेर्मे कोपमा भवेल्लोके। धन्योऽहं धन्योऽहं धन्यो धन्यः पुनः पुनर्धन्यः॥

Blessed am I, blessed, for there is nothing to compare with my great bliss! Blessed am I, blessed, blessed, blessed, again and again blessed!

Chapter 14 · Verse 63

14.63

अहो पुण्यमहो पुण्यं फलितं फलितं दृढम्। अस्य पुण्यस्य सम्पत्तेरहो वयमहो वयम्॥

O my merits, my merits, how enduringly they have borne fruit! Wonderful are we, the possessors of this great merit, wonderful!

Chapter 14 · Verse 64

14.64

अहो शास्त्रमहो शास्त्रमहो गुरुरहो गुरुः। अहो ज्ञानमहो ज्ञानमहो सुखमहो सुखम्॥

O how grand and true are the scriptures, the scriptures, O how grand and great is my teacher, my teacher! O how grand is this illumination, this illumination, O how grand is this bliss, this bliss!

Chapter 14 · Verse 65

14.65

ब्रह्मानन्दाभिधे ग्रन्थे चतुर्थोऽध्याय ईरितः। विद्यानन्दस्तदुत्पत्तिपर्यन्तोऽभ्यास इष्यताम्॥

This fourth chapter of the section called the ‘Bliss of Brahman’ describes the ‘Bliss of Knowledge’. Until that bliss is attained a man should engage himself in the practice of the contemplation of Brahman.

Chapter 15

Chapter 15 · Verse 1

15.1

अथात्र विषयानन्दो ब्रह्मानन्दांशरूपभाक्। निरूप्यते द्वारभूतस्तदंशत्वं श्रुतिर्जगौ॥

Now, in this Chapter is described the bliss which is derived from (the contact of the mind with) external objects, which may be called a door to the bliss of Brahman and an aspect of it. The Śruti has established that it is an aspect of that bliss.

Chapter 15 · Verse 2

15.2

एषोऽस्य परमानन्दो योऽखण्डैकरसात्मकः। अन्यानि भूतान्येतस्य मात्रामेवोपभुञ्जते॥

The Śruti says that this is the supreme bliss which is indivisible and homogeneous, it is Brahman Himself and that other beings (individuated by Avidyā) enjoy only a fraction of it.

Chapter 15 · Verse 3

15.3

शान्ता घोरास्तथा मूढा मनसो वृत्तयस्त्रिधा। वैराग्यं क्षान्तिरौदार्यमित्याद्याः शान्तवृत्तयः॥

The mental modifications are of three kinds: serene (Sāttvikā, śāntā), agitated (Rājasikā, ghorā) and dull (Tāmasikā, mūḍhā). The Sāttvikā modifications are detachment, fortitude, liberality and so forth.

Chapter 15 · Verse 4

15.4

तृष्णा स्नेहो रागलोभावित्याद्या घोरवृत्तयः। संमोहोभयमित्याद्याः कथिता मूढवृत्तयः॥

The Rājasikā modifications are thirst and love for objects, attachment (to them as if they were real), greed and so forth. The Tāmasikā modifications are said to be delusion, fear and so forth.

Chapter 15 · Verse 5

15.5

वृत्तिष्वेतासु सर्वासु ब्रह्मणश्चित्स्वभावता। प्रतिबिम्बति शान्तासु सुखं च प्रतिबिम्बति॥

The consciousness aspect of Brahman is reflected in all these modifications, but in the Sāttvikā modifications alone joy also is reflected.

Chapter 15 · Verse 6

15.6

रूपं रूपं बभूवासौ प्रतिरूप इति श्रुतिः। उपमा सूर्यकेत्वादि सूत्रयामास सूत्रकृत्॥

The Śruti says that entering into different bodies the supreme Self assumes different forms. Vyāsa , the author of the Brahma-Sūtras, wrote the Sūtra which illustrates the entry of Brahman into the bodies by the example of the sun (taking different forms) when reflected in different water-vessels.

Chapter 15 · Verse 7

15.7

एक एव हि भूतात्मा भूते भूते व्यवस्थितः। एकधा बहुधा चैव दृश्यते जलचन्द्रवत्॥

(Another Śruti says): 'The supreme Self, though one only, exists in every object. Like the moon reflected in water, though one It appears as many'.

Chapter 15 · Verse 8

15.8

जले प्रविष्टश्चन्द्रोऽयमस्पष्टः कलुषे जले। विस्पष्टो निर्मले तद्वद्द्वेधा ब्रह्मापि वृत्तिषु॥

The moon which is reflected in water is faint in muddy water and clear in pure water. Similarly Brahman is two-fold according to the quality of the Vṛttis (modification) of the mind.

Chapter 15 · Verse 9

15.9

घोरमूढासु मालिन्यात्सुखांशस्य तिरस्कृतिः। ईषन्नैर्मल्यतस्तत्र चिदंशप्रतिबिम्बनम्॥

Because of the preponderance of impurities of the Rājasikā and Tāmasikā Vṛttis, the blissfulness of Brahman is obscured; but because of their slight purity the consciousness of Brahman is reflected.

Chapter 15 · Verse 10

15.10

यद्वापि निर्मले नीरे वह्नेरौष्ण्यस्य संक्रमः। न प्रकाशस्य तद्वत्स्याच्चिन्मात्रोद्भूतिरत्र च॥

Or as in pure water when heated there is the transmission of heat of the fire and not its light, similarly in the Vṛttis (in which Rajas and Tamas predominate) there is the manifestation of consciousness only (not the bliss).

Chapter 15 · Verse 11

15.11

काष्ठे त्वौष्ण्यप्रकाशौ द्वावुद्भवं गच्छतो यथा। शान्तासु सुखचैतन्ये तथैवोद्भूतिमाप्नुतः॥

But as in (a piece of burning) wood both heat and light are manifested, similarly in the Sāttvikā Vṛttis both consciousness and bliss are manifested.

Chapter 15 · Verse 12

15.12

वस्तुस्वरूपमाश्रित्य व्यवस्था तूभयोः समा। अनुभूत्यनुसारेण कल्प्यते हि नियामकम्॥

These two illustrations make it clear that it is the nature of things which determines what kind of manifestation they may give and it is by experience that these properties are established.

Chapter 15 · Verse 13

15.13

न घोरासु न मूढासु सुखानुभव ईक्ष्यते। शान्तास्वपि क्वचित्कश्चित्सुखातिशय ईश्यताम्॥

Neither in Rājasikā nor in Tāmasikā Vṛttis the experience of bliss is seen but in Sāttvikā Vṛttis experience of happiness is seen to a greater or lesser degree.

Chapter 15 · Verse 14

15.14

गृहक्षेत्रादिविषये यदा कामो भवेत्तदा। राजसस्यास्य कामस्य घोरत्वात्तत्र नो सुखम्॥

When a man has desires for houses, lands and other objects then because of the agitated quality of this desire which is an effect of Rajas, there is no happiness for him.

Chapter 15 · Verse 15

15.15

सिद्ध्येन्न वेत्यस्ति दुःखमसिद्धौ तद्विवर्धते। प्रतिबन्धे भवेत्क्रोधो द्वेषो वा प्रतिबन्धकः॥

There is misery in thinking whether it will succeed; in failure this misery increases; when there are obstacles to success, anger arises or if opposed, hatred.

Chapter 15 · Verse 16

15.16

अशक्यश्चेत्प्रतीकारो विषदः स्यात्स तानसः। क्रोधादिषु महादुःखं सुखशङ्कापि दूरतः॥

If the opposition is too formidable to be overcome, there is despair; that is born of Tamas. In anger etc., there is great misery; indeed even the chance of happiness is remote.

Chapter 15 · Verse 17

15.17

काम्यलाभे हर्षवृत्तिः शान्ता तत्र महत्सुखम्। भोगे महत्तरं लाभप्रसक्तावीषदेव हि॥

With the acquisition of the desired object the pleasing Vṛtti is calmed and there is great happiness; and in actual enjoyment, the happiness is greater. Even in the prospect of acquiring it, there is some happiness.

Chapter 15 · Verse 18

15.18

महत्तमं विरक्तौ तु विद्यानन्दे तदीरितम्। एवं क्षान्तौ तथौदार्ये क्रोधलोभनिवारणात्॥

But the greatest happiness is the outcome of detachment. This subject has been dealt with in the Chapter on the ‘Bliss of Knowledge’. Like this there is happiness in fortitude as well as in liberality, because there are no anger and greed.

Chapter 15 · Verse 19

15.19

यद्यत्सुखं भवेत्तत्तद्ब्रह्मैव प्रतिबिम्बनात्। वृत्तिष्वन्तर्मुखा स्वस्य निर्विघ्नं प्रतिबिम्बनम्॥

Whatever happiness is experienced it is Brahman alone because it is a reflection of the bliss of Brahman. When the Vṛtti is directed inward or is withdrawn, the reflection of bliss is unobstructed.

Chapter 15 · Verse 20

15.20

सत्ता चितिः सुखं चेति स्वभावा ब्रह्मणस्त्रयः। मृच्छिलादिषु सत्तैव व्यज्यते नेतरद्द्वयम्॥

Existence, consciousness and bliss – these are the threefold nature of Brahman. In objects like clay, stone and so forth, only existence is manifest, whereas the other two are not.

Chapter 15 · Verse 21

15.21

सत्ता चितिर्द्वयं व्यक्तं धीवृत्त्योर्घोरमूढयोः। शान्तवृत्तौ त्रयं व्यक्तं मिश्रं ब्रह्मेत्थमीरितम्॥

Both existence and consciousness are manifest in the Rājasikā and Tāmasikā Vṛttis of the intellect and all the three are manifest in the Sāttvikā Vṛttis. Brahman associated with the world including the Vṛttis is thus described.

Chapter 15 · Verse 22

15.22

अमिश्रं ज्ञानयोगाभ्यां तौ च पूर्वमुदीरितौ। आद्येऽध्याये योगचिन्ता ज्ञानमध्यायोर्द्वयोः॥

Brahman not associated with the world is comprehended by knowledge and Yoga. They have been spoken of earlier, the topic of Yoga in Chapter 11 and knowledge in the next two chapters.

Chapter 15 · Verse 23

15.23

असत्ता जाड्यदुःखे द्वे मायारूपं त्रयं त्विदम्। असत्ता नरशृङ्गादौ जाड्यं काष्ठशिलादिषु॥

The two, absence of consciousness and misery, and non-existence – these are the three forms of Māyā. Non-existence is illustrated by such expressions as ‘the horns of a man’; absence of consciousness is seen in such objects as wood, stone etc.

Chapter 15 · Verse 24

15.24

घोरमूढधियोर्दुःखमेवं माया विजृम्भिता। शान्तादि बुद्धिवृत्त्यैक्यान्मिश्रं ब्रह्मेति कीर्तितम्॥

There is misery in the Rājasikā and Tāmasikā Vṛttis. Thus Māyā is manifested. Because of His identification with the Vṛttis of the intellect, which are Sāttvikā, Rājasikā and Tāmasikā, Brahman is called ‘associated Brahman’ i.e., Brahman is associated with the world.

Chapter 15 · Verse 25

15.25

एवं स्थितेऽत्र यो ब्रह्म ध्यातुमिच्छेत्पुमानसौ। नृशृङ्गादिमुपेक्षेत शिष्टं ध्यायेद्यथायथम्॥

Such being the nature of Māyā and Brahman, the man who wishes to meditate on Brahman should ignore the objects which have no existence (such as the horns of a man) and concentrate properly on other objects.

Chapter 15 · Verse 26

15.26

शिलादौ नामरूपे द्वे त्यक्त्वा सन्मात्रचिन्तनम्। त्यक्त्वा दुःखं घोरमूढधियोः सच्चिद्विचिन्तनम्॥

In stone etc., he should reject both name and form and meditate on existence; in Rājasikā and Tāmasikā Vṛttis he should reject the misery (which is associated with them) and meditate on existence and consciousness.

Chapter 15 · Verse 27

15.27

शान्तासु सच्चिदानन्दांस्त्रीनप्येवं विचिन्तयेत्। कनिष्ठमध्यमोत्कृष्टास्तिस्रश्चिन्ताः क्रमादिमाः॥

And in the Sāttvikā Vṛttis he should contemplate on all the three – existence, consciousness and bliss. These three kinds of contemplation are successively called inferior, middling and superior contemplations.

Chapter 15 · Verse 28

15.28

मन्दस्य व्यवहारेऽपि मिश्रब्रह्मणि चिन्तनम्। उत्कृष्टं व्यक्तुमेवात्र विषयानन्द ईरितः॥

Even for a man of dull intellect meditation on the characteristics of Brahman is good. To tell this only ‘the Bliss of Objects’ is described here.

Chapter 15 · Verse 29

15.29

औदासीन्ये तु धीवृत्तेः शैथिल्यादुत्तमोत्तमम्। चिन्तनं वासनानन्दे ध्यानमुक्तं चतुर्विधम्॥

After having had enough of enjoyments, when the mental modifications become indifferent to objects and become detached, the contemplation regarding the bliss of impressions arise, which is the highest. Thus are the four kinds of contemplation on Brahman described.

Chapter 15 · Verse 30

15.30

न ध्यानं ज्ञानयोगाभ्यां ब्रह्मविद्यैव सा खलु। ध्यानेनैकाग्र्यमापन्ने चित्ते विद्या स्थिरीभवेत्॥

As in these four types of meditation there is an admixture of knowledge and Yoga they are not mere meditations; but should be considered as a (direct means of achieving) the knowledge of Brahman itself. The mind being concentrated by meditation, this knowledge of Brahman becomes steady.

Chapter 15 · Verse 31

15.31

विद्यायां सच्चिदानन्दा अखण्डैकरसात्मताम्। प्राप्य भान्ति न भेदेन भेदकोपाधिवर्जनात्॥

In steady knowledge, existence, consciousness and bliss shine as a single homogeneous entity and not as separate entities, their difference having disappeared with the disappearance of their Upādhis or adjuncts.

Chapter 15 · Verse 32

15.32

शान्ता घोराः शिलाद्याश्च भेदकोपाधयो मताः। योगाद् विवेकतो वैषमुपाधीनामपाकृतिः॥

It is said that the adjuncts creating difference are the Sāttvikā, Rājasikā and Tāmasikā Vṛttis. Through either Yoga or discrimination these disturbing Vṛttis are removed.

Chapter 15 · Verse 33

15.33

निरुपाधिब्रह्मतत्त्वे भासमाने स्वयंप्रभे। अद्वैते त्रिपुटी नास्ति भूमानन्दोऽत उच्यते॥

When the associationless, self-luminous and secondless Brahman is grasped or known, there is then no triad of knower, knowing and known. So it is called infinite bliss.

Chapter 15 · Verse 34

15.34

ब्रह्मानन्द अभिधे ग्रन्थे पञ्चमोऽध्याय ईरितः। विषयानन्द एतेन द्वारेणान्तः प्रवेश्यताम्॥

In this, the fifth chapter of the section called ‘the Bliss of Brahman’, ‘the Bliss of Objects’ has been dealt with. Through this door enter (i.e., into the bliss of Brahman).

Chapter 15 · Verse 35

15.35

प्रीयाद्धरिहरोऽनेन ब्रह्मानन्देन सर्वदा। पायाच्च प्राणिनः सर्वान्स्वाश्रितां शुद्धमानसान्॥

May the Lord who is both Hari (Viṣṇu) and Hara (Śiva) ever be pleased by this ‘Bliss of Brahman’ and may He protect all creatures who take refuge in Him and are pure in heart.
